anglo_am.name: Anglo-Americans
anglo_am.note: United States interior; northward shift into a warmer Canada and Alaska. Mars: early PIONEER and VANTEC staff
anglo_am.strong: Illinoia Sector, Concordia Union Territory, Columbia Commonwealth
anglo_am.desc: The Anglo-Americans are the people of the United States interior, and in 2240 they number about 933 million. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak American English, and most are Protestant, Catholic or secular. They are strongest in Illinoia Sector, Concordia Union Territory, Columbia Commonwealth. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

hannorth.name: Northern Han
hannorth.note: North China plain, Manchuria; settlers across the Amur. Mars: first-wave Chinese agency crews
hannorth.strong: Zhili Commonwealth, Shandong Circuit, Henan Circuit
hannorth.desc: The people of North China plain, Manchuria are the Northern Han, about 453 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. They speak Mandarin, and most are Secular, folk religion or Buddhist. Their strongholds are Zhili Commonwealth, Shandong Circuit, Henan Circuit. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

brazilian.name: Brazilians
brazilian.strong: Sao Paulo Captaincy, Minas Gerais Captaincy, Planalto Federal District
brazilian.desc: In Brazil live the Brazilians, a people of about 335 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Brazilian Portuguese is their language, and most of them are Catholic, Evangelical or Spiritist. Their strongholds are Sao Paulo Captaincy, Minas Gerais Captaincy, Planalto Federal District. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

hindustani.name: Hindustanis (Hindi-Urdu)
hindustani.note: Ganges plain, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh. Mars: second-wave labour settlers
hindustani.strong: Uttar Pradesh, Delhi Commonwealth, Deccan Commonwealth
hindustani.desc: The people of Ganges plain, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh are the Hindustanis (Hindi-Urdu), about 307 million strong in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Hindi-Urdu. In faith most are Hindu or Muslim. Their strongholds are Uttar Pradesh, Delhi Commonwealth, Deccan Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

mexican.name: Mexicans (Mestizo)
mexican.note: Mexico; the US Southwest. Mars: Hellas farm crews
mexican.strong: Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth, Zacatecas-Jalisco, Las Californias Sector
mexican.desc: The people of Mexico are the Mexicans (Mestizo), about 290 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Mexican Spanish is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth, Zacatecas-Jalisco, Las Californias Sector. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

japanese.name: Japanese
japanese.note: Japanese islands, highland-shifted. Mars: SYNTRIX automation towns
japanese.strong: Kanto Commonwealth, Hiroshima Prefecture, Hokkaido Prefecture
japanese.desc: The Japanese are the people of the Japanese islands, and in 2240 they number about 287 million. Their islands kept their own language, emperors and culture through the long centuries of East Asian history. They speak Japanese, and most are Shinto and Buddhist or secular. They are strongest in Kanto Commonwealth, Hiroshima Prefecture, Hokkaido Prefecture. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

russian.name: Russians
russian.note: European Russia; large share of the 2240 Siberian boom. Mars: Arctic-trained crews of the 2090s
russian.desc: The Russians are the people of European Russia, and in 2240 they number about 283 million. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. They speak Russian, and most are Orthodox Christian or largely secular. They are strongest in Muscovy Commonwealth, Iset Commonwealth, Meshchera. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

colombian.name: Colombians and Venezuelans
colombian.strong: Bogota Capital District, Guarico Department, Barinas Department
colombian.desc: In Andean north, Llanos live the Colombians and Venezuelans, a people of about 180 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Colombian and Venezuelan Spanish is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Bogota Capital District, Guarico Department, Barinas Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

french.name: French
french.desc: In France, Wallonia, Romandy live the French, a people of about 134 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. They speak French, and most are Secular or Catholic heritage. They are strongest in Ile-de-France Commonwealth, Isere-Drome, Dordogne-Aveyron. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

turkish.name: Turks
turkish.strong: Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet, Ankara Capital Vilayet, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet
turkish.desc: In Anatolia, Thrace live the Turks, a people of about 119 million in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. They speak Turkish, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet, Ankara Capital Vilayet, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

persian.name: Persians
persian.strong: Alborz Commonwealth, Fars Satrapy, Yazd-Isfahan Satrapy
persian.desc: In the Iranian plateau live the Persians, a people of about 110 million in 2240. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. They speak Persian, and most are Shia Muslim. Their strongholds are Alborz Commonwealth, Fars Satrapy, Yazd-Isfahan Satrapy. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

german.name: Germans
german.note: Germany, Austria, Swiss plateau. Mars: VANTEC foundry towns, nationalised 2187
german.desc: The people of the Germany, Austria, Swiss plateau are the Germans, about 109 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Their language is German. In faith most are Protestant or Catholic and secular. Their strongholds are Bavaria Kreis, Hesse Kreis, Trentino-Turin. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

hansw.name: Southwestern Han
hansw.strong: Chengdu Commonwealth, Chongqing Circuit, Guizhou Circuit
hansw.desc: In Sichuan basin, Chongqing, Yunnan-Guizhou live the Southwestern Han, a people of about 107 million in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. Southwestern Mandarin is their language, and most of them are Secular, folk religion or Buddhist. Their strongholds are Chengdu Commonwealth, Chongqing Circuit, Guizhou Circuit. Shanghai, Tianjin and the old coastal plain went under the rising sea, and their people moved inland, to the hills and the new northern cities.

m_austral.name: Southern highlanders
m_austral.note: Cimmeria, Sirenum, Aonia: thin, cold farm country
m_austral.language: Southern Highland speech (Russian and English roots)
m_austral.strong: South Memnonia, South Eridania II, Ma'adim
m_austral.desc: The Southern highlanders are the Martian-born people of Cimmeria, Sirenum, Aonia, about 102 million in 2240. They speak Southern Highland speech (Russian and English roots), and most hold to Orthodox or secular. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through South Memnonia, South Eridania II, Ma'adim.

rioplatense.name: Rioplatenses
rioplatense.strong: Rio de la Plata Commonwealth, La Pampa, Cordoba
rioplatense.desc: In Argentina, Uruguay live the Rioplatenses, a people of about 100 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Rioplatense Spanish is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic or secular. Their strongholds are Rio de la Plata Commonwealth, La Pampa, Cordoba. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

spanish.name: Spaniards
spanish.desc: In Castile, Andalusia live the Spaniards, a people of about 99 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Spanish is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic or secular. They are strongest in Castilian Commonwealth, Caceres-Badajoz, Zaragoza-Teruel. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

korean.name: Koreans
korean.note: Korean peninsula; in the Russian Far East. Mars: SYNTRIX and shipyard workers
korean.strong: Han River Commonwealth, South Hamgyong Province, Liaoning Circuit
korean.desc: In the Korean peninsula live the Koreans, a people of about 99 million in 2240. Their Korean nation has lived on the same peninsula, with its own language and alphabet, for well over a thousand years. They speak Korean, and most are Secular, Protestant or Buddhist. They are strongest in Han River Commonwealth, South Hamgyong Province, Liaoning Circuit. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

canadian.name: Anglo-Canadians
canadian.note: Ontario, Prairies, British Columbia; the new farm belt up to the Arctic Reach
canadian.strong: Upper Canada, Columbia Commonwealth, Absaroka Sector
canadian.desc: The people of Ontario, Prairies, British Columbia are the Anglo-Canadians, about 93 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak Canadian English, and most are Secular or Christian. They are strongest in Upper Canada, Columbia Commonwealth, Absaroka Sector. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

min.name: Min Chinese
min.strong: Fujian Circuit, Pearl River Commonwealth, Yangtze Commonwealth
min.desc: In Fujian, Taiwan live the Min Chinese, a people of about 87 million in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. Hokkien is their language, and most of them are Folk religion (Mazu) or Buddhist. Their strongholds are Fujian Circuit, Pearl River Commonwealth, Yangtze Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

gulf.name: Najdi and Hejazi Arabs
gulf.note: Arabian interior and Hejaz; its coasts drowned or abandoned for heat
gulf.strong: Najd Commonwealth, Makkah Emirate, Eastern Emirate
gulf.desc: The people of Arabian interior and Hejaz are the Najdi and Hejazi Arabs, about 85 million strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Their language is Najdi and Hejazi Arabic. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Najd Commonwealth, Makkah Emirate, Eastern Emirate. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_rockylaunch.name: Rocky Mountain Launch Clans
f_rockylaunch.note: Anglo and Korean families of the Colorado spaceports
f_rockylaunch.language: American English and Korean (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_rockylaunch.faith: Protestant and Secular families; many secular
f_rockylaunch.desc: In Concordia Union Territory, Anglo-Americans and Koreans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Rocky Mountain Launch Clans. At home they speak American English and Korean, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Protestant by family, and many are secular. About 82 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Concordia Union Territory. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

marathi.name: Marathis
marathi.desc: In Maharashtra live the Marathis, a people of about 79 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Marathi. In faith most are Hindu or Buddhist. They are strongest in Deccan Commonwealth, Kaveri Commonwealth, Gujarat. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

m_hellasian.name: Hellasians
m_hellasian.note: Rim of the Hellas sea, Noachis, Hesperia
m_hellasian.desc: The Hellasians are the Martian-born people of Rim of the Hellas sea, Noachis, Hesperia, about 79 million in 2240. They speak Hellasian (Portuguese and Spanish roots), and most hold to Catholic or secular. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Tyrrhenus, Gale, Cimmeria.

cantonese.name: Cantonese
cantonese.strong: Pearl River Commonwealth, Guangxi Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit
cantonese.desc: The Cantonese are the people of the Lingnan uplands, and in 2240 they number about 73 million. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. Cantonese is their language, and most of them are Folk religion, Buddhist or Christian. They are strongest in Pearl River Commonwealth, Guangxi Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

wu.name: Wu Chinese
wu.note: Lower Yangtze above the drowned delta
wu.desc: The people of the Lower Yangtze above the drowned delta are the Wu Chinese, about 72 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. They speak Wu (Shanghainese), and most are Secular, Buddhist or folk religion. They are strongest in Yangtze Commonwealth, Fujian Circuit. Shanghai, Tianjin and the old coastal plain went under the rising sea, and their people moved inland, to the hills and the new northern cities.

quebecois.name: Québécois
quebecois.note: St Lawrence and the Laurentian north
quebecois.strong: Ottawa Crown District, New England Sector, Columbia Commonwealth
quebecois.desc: In the St Lawrence and the Laurentian north live the Québécois, a people of about 71 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Quebec French. In faith most are Secular or Catholic heritage. Their strongholds are Ottawa Crown District, New England Sector, Columbia Commonwealth. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

italian.name: Italians
italian.desc: The Italians are the people of Italy, and in 2240 they number about 71 million. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Italian is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Trentino-Turin, Potenza-Foggia, Latium Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

maghrebi.name: Maghrebi Arabs
maghrebi.note: Maghreb coast; large communities in France, Spain and Italy
maghrebi.strong: Algiers Commonwealth, Ouargla Wilaya, Mizdah Wilaya
maghrebi.desc: The people of the Maghreb coast are the Maghrebi Arabs, about 65 million strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Their language is Maghrebi Arabic (Darija), French. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Algiers Commonwealth, Ouargla Wilaya, Mizdah Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

ukrainian.name: Ukrainians
ukrainian.desc: The people of Ukraine are the Ukrainians, about 64 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Ukrainian is their language, and most of them are Orthodox and Greek Catholic. They are strongest in Dnieper Commonwealth, Dnipropetrovsk, Minsk-Gomel. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

punjabi.name: Punjabis
punjabi.strong: Ravi Commonwealth, Delhi Commonwealth, Himachal Pradesh
punjabi.desc: In Punjab live the Punjabis, a people of about 63 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Punjabi, and most are Sikh, Muslim or Hindu. They are strongest in Ravi Commonwealth, Delhi Commonwealth, Himachal Pradesh. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

m_arabian.name: Arabians (Martian)
m_arabian.note: Arabia Terra, Meridiani: the old industrial belt seized from VANTEC in 2187
m_arabian.language: Arabian Martian (Hindi, Arabic and English roots)
m_arabian.desc: The Arabians (Martian) are the Martian-born people of Arabia Terra, Meridiani, about 63 million in 2240. They speak Arabian Martian (Hindi, Arabic and English roots), and most hold to Secular or Muslim and Hindu minorities. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Sinus Sabaeus, Sabaea, Margaritifer.

egyptian.name: Egyptians
egyptian.note: Nile valley above the drowned delta
egyptian.strong: Delta Commonwealth, South Sinai Nome, New Valley Nome
egyptian.desc: The Egyptians are the people of the Nile valley above the drowned delta, and in 2240 they number about 63 million. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Egyptian Arabic, and most are Sunni Muslim or Coptic Christian. They are strongest in Delta Commonwealth, South Sinai Nome, New Valley Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

anglo_au.name: Anglo-Australians
anglo_au.desc: In Australian south-east and south-west, Aotearoa live the Anglo-Australians, a people of about 63 million in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak Australian English, and most are Secular or Christian. They are strongest in Port Phillip, Cumberland, Moreton Commonwealth. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

mongol.name: Mongols
mongol.strong: Inner Mongolia Aimag, Zhili Commonwealth, Gansu Circuit
mongol.desc: The Mongols are the people of Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, and in 2240 they number about 57 million. Their ancestors once rode with the largest land empire in history, and the steppe still shapes their way of life. Mongolian is their language, and most of them are Tibetan Buddhist or shamanist. They are strongest in Inner Mongolia Aimag, Zhili Commonwealth, Gansu Circuit. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

andean.name: Andean Mestizos
andean.strong: Amazonas-Caqueta Department, Lima Commonwealth, Santa Cruz March
andean.desc: In Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia lowland cities live the Andean Mestizos, a people of about 55 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Andean Spanish. In faith most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Amazonas-Caqueta Department, Lima Commonwealth, Santa Cruz March. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

telugu.name: Telugus
telugu.desc: In Andhra and Telangana live the Telugus, a people of about 55 million in 2240. Their Dravidian language is older in India than the Indo-Aryan ones, with a literature reaching back two thousand years. Their language is Telugu. In faith most are Hindu. Their strongholds are Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Deccan Commonwealth. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

m_tharsian.name: Tharsians
m_tharsian.note: Tharsis highlands: the first terraforming crews' descendants, heart of the Sovereignty
m_tharsian.language: Tharsian Creole (Mandarin, English and Russian roots)
m_tharsian.desc: The Tharsians are the Martian-born people of the Tharsis highlands, about 54 million in 2240. They speak Tharsian Creole (Mandarin, English and Russian roots), and most hold to Secular Martian civic faith. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Pavonis, South Memnonia II, Bosporos.

levantine.name: Levantine Arabs
levantine.note: Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Palestine. Mars: Arabia Terra engineers
levantine.strong: Damascus Capital District, Ma'an, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet
levantine.desc: In Syria, Lebanon, Jordan, Palestine live the Levantine Arabs, a people of about 50 million in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Levantine Arabic, and most are Sunni Muslim or Christian. They are strongest in Damascus Capital District, Ma'an, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

kongo.name: Kongo and Lingala peoples
kongo.desc: The Kongo and Lingala peoples are the people of Lower Congo, Kinshasa, Brazzaville, and in 2240 they number about 49 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Kikongo is their language, and most of them are Christian or Kimbanguist. They are strongest in Pool Commonwealth, Malanje-Bie, Kongo Central. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

polish.name: Poles
polish.strong: Vistula Commonwealth, Banska Bystrica March, Central Bohemian March
polish.desc: In Poland live the Poles, a people of about 48 million in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Their language is Polish. In faith most are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Vistula Commonwealth, Banska Bystrica March, Central Bohemian March. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

sudanese.name: Sudanese Arabs and Nubians
sudanese.strong: Al Qadarif Nome, North Kordofan Nome, Tigray-Gash-Barka
sudanese.desc: The Sudanese Arabs and Nubians are the people of Middle Nile, Kordofan, Darfur, and in 2240 they number about 47 million. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Sudanese Arabic is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Al Qadarif Nome, North Kordofan Nome, Tigray-Gash-Barka. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

thai.name: Thai
thai.strong: Chao Phraya Commonwealth, Shan State, Vientiane-Savannakhet
thai.desc: In Chao Phraya highlands, Isan live the Thai, a people of about 45 million in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. Thai is their language, and most of them are Theravada Buddhist. They are strongest in Chao Phraya Commonwealth, Shan State, Vientiane-Savannakhet. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

malay.name: Malays
malay.desc: In Malaya, Sumatra coasts, Borneo live the Malays, a people of about 44 million in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Malay. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Johor, Klang Commonwealth, Deli Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

centroamerican.name: Central Americans
centroamerican.strong: South Caribbean Coast Canton, Peten Canton, Olancho Canton
centroamerican.desc: The people of Isthmus are the Central Americans, about 44 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Central American Spanish. In faith most are Catholic or Evangelical. Their strongholds are South Caribbean Coast Canton, Peten Canton, Olancho Canton. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

first_nations.name: First Nations and Native Americans
first_nations.strong: Upper Canada, Superior Sector, Salish Commonwealth
first_nations.desc: The people of Canadian Shield, Plains, Southwest are the First Nations and Native Americans, about 43 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Cree. In faith most are Traditional or Christian. Their strongholds are Upper Canada, Superior Sector, Salish Commonwealth. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

kazakh.name: Kazakhs
kazakh.note: Kazakh steppe; spreading north into a warmer western Siberia
kazakh.desc: The people of the Kazakh steppe are the Kazakhs, about 43 million strong in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Kazakh is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim or secular. They are strongest in Almaty, Tashkent Capital District, Karaganda. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

tswana.name: Sotho-Tswana
tswana.desc: In Highveld, Botswana, Lesotho live the Sotho-Tswana, a people of about 42 million in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Setswana. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Highveld Commonwealth, Free State, Limpopo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

m_boreal.name: Boreal coasters
m_boreal.note: Shores of the northern sea: fishing, kelp and shipping towns
m_boreal.desc: The people of the Shores of the northern sea are the Boreal coasters, about 42 million strong, born on Mars of the settlers who came in the 2060s and after. They speak Boreal Coast speech, and most hold to Secular or sea cults. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Jezero, Nilosyrtis, Utopia Rupes.

sibiryak.name: Sibiryaks (new Siberians)
sibiryak.note: Born in the Siberian boom: Russian, Central Asian, Chinese and Korean roots mixed in the new Yenisei, Angara and Lena cities
sibiryak.language: Siberian Russian with Chinese, Korean and Turkic loanwords
sibiryak.desc: The Sibiryaks (new Siberians) are the people of Baikalia, and in 2240 they number about 41 million. Siberian Russian with Chinese, Korean and Turkic loanwords is their language, and most of them are Secular, Orthodox, Buddhist or Muslim. They are strongest in Baikalia, Yeniseia, Kuznetsk. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

english.name: English
english.strong: Home Counties Commonwealth, North Yorkshire, Ile-de-France Commonwealth
english.desc: The English are the people of England, and in 2240 they number about 41 million. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Their language is English. In faith most are Secular or Anglican. They are strongest in Home Counties Commonwealth, North Yorkshire, Ile-de-France Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

hausa.name: Hausa
hausa.strong: Bauchi State, Abuja Federal Territory, Tahoua-Tillaberi
hausa.desc: The people of Northern Nigeria, Niger are the Hausa, about 39 million strong in 2240. They are a Chadic people of the Sahel, long-distance traders whose language became the common tongue of West Africa's interior. Their language is Hausa. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Bauchi State, Abuja Federal Territory, Tahoua-Tillaberi. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

scandinavian.name: Scandinavians
scandinavian.note: Sweden, Norway, Denmark; settlers in ice-free Greenland
scandinavian.desc: The people of Sweden, Norway, Denmark are the Scandinavians, about 39 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Their language is Swedish. In faith most are Lutheran heritage or largely secular. They are strongest in Dalarna, Oppland, Malar Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

tamil.name: Tamils
tamil.strong: Tamil Nadu, Kaveri Commonwealth, Andhra Pradesh
tamil.desc: The Tamils are the people of Tamil Nadu, and in 2240 they number about 37 million. Their Dravidian language is older in India than the Indo-Aryan ones, with a literature reaching back two thousand years. Their language is Tamil. In faith most are Hindu, Christian or Muslim. Their strongholds are Tamil Nadu, Kaveri Commonwealth, Andhra Pradesh. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

serbcroat.name: South Slavs (Serbo-Croatian)
serbcroat.strong: Belgrade Federal District, Banja Luka, Pomoravski-Berat
serbcroat.desc: The South Slavs (Serbo-Croatian) are the people of Western Balkans, and in 2240 they number about 37 million. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. They speak Serbo-Croatian, and most are Orthodox (Serbs) or Catholic (Croats). They are strongest in Belgrade Federal District, Banja Luka, Pomoravski-Berat. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

kannada.name: Kannadigas
kannada.strong: Kaveri Commonwealth, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu
kannada.desc: The Kannadigas are the people of Karnataka, and in 2240 they number about 37 million. Their Dravidian language is older in India than the Indo-Aryan ones, with a literature reaching back two thousand years. Their language is Kannada. In faith most are Hindu or Lingayat. Their strongholds are Kaveri Commonwealth, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

chilean.name: Chileans
chilean.note: Chile; the largest group on the Antarctic Peninsula
chilean.strong: La Pampa, Rio Negro, La Rioja
chilean.desc: The people of Chile are the Chileans, about 35 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Chilean Spanish. In faith most are Roman Catholic or Evangelical. Their strongholds are La Pampa, Rio Negro, La Rioja. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

pashtun.name: Pashtuns
pashtun.note: Afghan south and east, Pakistani frontier
pashtun.strong: Indus Capital Territory, Ravi Commonwealth, Sindh March
pashtun.desc: In Afghan south and east, Pakistani frontier live the Pashtuns, a people of about 35 million in 2240. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. Pashto is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Indus Capital Territory, Ravi Commonwealth, Sindh March. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

hisp_carib.name: Dominicans and Puerto Ricans
hisp_carib.desc: The people of Eastern Hispaniola, Puerto Rico are the Dominicans and Puerto Ricans, about 33 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Caribbean Spanish is their language, and most of them are Catholic or Evangelical. They are strongest in Havana League Seat, Borinquen Sector. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

m_elysian.name: Elysians
m_elysian.desc: The Elysians are the Martian-born people of Elysium and Aeolis, about 33 million in 2240. They speak Elysian (Japanese and Korean roots), and most hold to Secular or Shinto-Buddhist. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Cerberus, Zephyria, Phlegra.

bengali.name: Bengalis
bengali.note: Bengal, pushed inland by the drowned delta into Assam, Bihar and Myanmar
bengali.strong: Ganga Delta Commonwealth, West Bengal, Jharkhand
bengali.desc: The Bengalis are the people of Bengal, and in 2240 they number about 32 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Bengali, and most are Muslim or Hindu. Their strongholds are Ganga Delta Commonwealth, West Bengal, Jharkhand. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

m_marineris.name: Mariners (Valles folk)
m_marineris.note: Valles Marineris canyon cities, Lunae and Xanthe
m_marineris.desc: The people of Valles Marineris canyon cities, Lunae and Xanthe are the Mariners (Valles folk), about 31 million strong, born on Mars of the settlers who came in the 2060s and after. They speak Mariner Creole, and most hold to Secular or Buddhist and Christian minorities. Their parents and grandparents fought in the war of independence that began in 2186; they think of themselves as Martians first, and of Earth as the old country that taxed them without a vote. Their heartland runs through Candor, Xanthe, Ganges.

african_am.name: African Americans
african_am.strong: Muskogee Sector, Orleans Sector, Franklin Sector
african_am.desc: The African Americans are the people of the American South, and in 2240 they number about 31 million. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Their language is American English. In faith most are Protestant (Black churches). Their strongholds are Muskogee Sector, Orleans Sector, Franklin Sector. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

gujarati.name: Gujaratis
gujarati.desc: In Gujarat live the Gujaratis, a people of about 31 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Gujarati, and most are Hindu, Jain or Muslim. Their strongholds are Gujarat, Deccan Commonwealth, Rajasthan. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

yoruba.name: Yoruba
yoruba.note: South-west Nigeria, Benin. Mars: Lagos-founded trading towns
yoruba.desc: The Yoruba are the people of South-west Nigeria, Benin, and in 2240 they number about 30 million. Their forebears built the forest kingdoms and city-states of the lower Niger, famous for bronze, trade and art. They speak Yoruba, and most are Christian, Muslim or Orisha faith. They are strongest in Abuja Federal Territory, Northern-Brong-Ahafo, Aram. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

reacher.name: Reachers (Arctic Canadians)
reacher.note: New Canadians of the thawed north: Anglo, Québécois, South Asian, Filipino, Latin American and Inuit descent
reacher.language: Northern English with French, Tagalog and Punjabi loanwords
reacher.strong: Salish Commonwealth, Upper Canada, Bow River Commonwealth
reacher.desc: In Salish Commonwealth live the Reachers (Arctic Canadians), a people of about 29 million in 2240. Northern English with French, Tagalog and Punjabi loanwords is their language, and most of them are Secular or mixed. Their strongholds are Salish Commonwealth, Upper Canada, Bow River Commonwealth. The thaw opened the north of their land to farming, and new towns grew where there had been permafrost.

greek.name: Greeks
greek.strong: Attic Commonwealth, Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet, East Macedonia and Thrace
greek.desc: The people of Greece, Cyprus are the Greeks, about 29 million strong in 2240. Their language has been written for more than three thousand years, longer than almost any other on Earth. Greek is their language, and most of them are Greek Orthodox. Their strongholds are Attic Commonwealth, Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet, East Macedonia and Thrace. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

sindhi.name: Sindhis
sindhi.note: Lower Indus above the new shore
sindhi.desc: The Sindhis are the people of the Lower Indus above the new shore, and in 2240 they number about 29 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Sindhi. In faith most are Muslim or Hindu. Their strongholds are Sindh March, Ravi Commonwealth, Gujarat. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

amazonian.name: Amazonian peoples
amazonian.language: Tupi-Guarani, Arawak and other Amazonian languages
amazonian.strong: Amazonas Captaincy, Amazonas-Caqueta Department, Para Captaincy
amazonian.desc: The people of Amazon forest are the Amazonian peoples, about 29 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Tupi-Guarani, Arawak and other Amazonian languages, and most are Traditional or Christian. Their strongholds are Amazonas Captaincy, Amazonas-Caqueta Department, Para Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

luba.name: Luba and Kasai peoples
luba.desc: The Luba and Kasai peoples are the people of Kasai, Katanga, and in 2240 they number about 29 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Tshiluba. In faith most are Christian. They are strongest in Katanga, Kasai-Oriental, Pool Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

fulani.name: Fula
fulani.strong: Siguiri Prefecture, Abuja Federal Territory, Mopti
fulani.desc: The Fula are the people of Sahel from Senegal to Cameroon, and in 2240 they number about 28 million. They are an Atlantic people of West Africa, herders, farmers and traders of the savannah and the coast. Their language is Fula (Fulfulde). In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Siguiri Prefecture, Abuja Federal Territory, Mopti. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

zulu.name: Zulu and Nguni
zulu.desc: The people of KwaZulu, Eswatini are the Zulu and Nguni, about 28 million strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. isiZulu is their language, and most of them are Christian or ancestral faith. Their strongholds are Highveld Commonwealth, Free State, Limpopo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

filipino.name: Tagalog and Luzon peoples
filipino.desc: The people of Luzon are the Tagalog and Luzon peoples, about 27 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Tagalog is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Maynila Commonwealth, Luzonia, Mait. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

sundanese.name: Sundanese
sundanese.desc: The Sundanese are the people of West Java, and in 2240 they number about 27 million. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Sundanese. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Java Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

hispanic_us.name: Hispanic Americans
hispanic_us.strong: Las Californias Sector, Tejas Sector, Coahuila
hispanic_us.desc: The people of Texas, California, Florida are the Hispanic Americans, about 27 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. American English is their language, and most of them are Catholic or Evangelical. They are strongest in Las Californias Sector, Tejas Sector, Coahuila. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

kurdish.name: Kurds
kurdish.strong: Two Rivers Commonwealth, East Azerbaijan, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet
kurdish.desc: The people of Kurdistan are the Kurds, about 26 million strong in 2240. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. They speak Kurmanji, Sorani, and most are Sunni Muslim, Yazidi or Alevi. They are strongest in Two Rivers Commonwealth, East Azerbaijan, Sanliurfa-Aleppo Vilayet. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

vietnamese.name: Vietnamese (Kinh)
vietnamese.note: Vietnamese highlands and coast above the drowned deltas
vietnamese.strong: Gia Lai, Luang Prabang, Hainan Circuit
vietnamese.desc: The people of Vietnamese highlands and coast above the drowned deltas are the Vietnamese (Kinh), about 26 million strong in 2240. They speak an Austroasiatic language, the tongue of the first rice farmers of mainland Southeast Asia. They speak Vietnamese, and most are Folk religion, Buddhist or Catholic. They are strongest in Gia Lai, Luang Prabang, Hainan Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

mesoamerican.name: Maya and Nahua peoples
mesoamerican.language: Nahuatl, Yucatec and other Maya languages
mesoamerican.strong: Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth, Peten Canton, Chiapas
mesoamerican.desc: In Southern Mexico, Guatemala live the Maya and Nahua peoples, a people of about 26 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Nahuatl is their language, and most of them are Catholic with Mesoamerican tradition. Their strongholds are Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth, Peten Canton, Chiapas. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

rajasthani.name: Rajasthanis
rajasthani.desc: In Rajasthan live the Rajasthanis, a people of about 26 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Rajasthani. In faith most are Hindu or Jain. Their strongholds are Rajasthan, Ravi Commonwealth, Sindh March. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

irish.name: Irish
irish.strong: Home Counties Commonwealth, North Yorkshire, Highland
irish.desc: The Irish are the people of Ireland, and in 2240 they number about 25 million. They are heirs of the Celtic peoples who once held most of western Europe and who held on longest at its Atlantic edge. Their language is English. In faith most are Roman Catholic or secular. They are strongest in Home Counties Commonwealth, North Yorkshire, Highland. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

mande.name: Mande peoples
mande.strong: Niger Bend Commonwealth, Siguiri Prefecture, Northern
mande.desc: The people of Mali, Guinea, Upper Niger are the Mande peoples, about 25 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Mande of the old Mali Empire, whose griots still keep its history in song. Bambara is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Niger Bend Commonwealth, Siguiri Prefecture, Northern. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

aboriginal.name: Aboriginal Australians
aboriginal.desc: The people of the Australian interior and north are the Aboriginal Australians, about 25 million strong in 2240. They are part of the oldest continuous culture on Earth, more than fifty thousand years on the Australian continent. Aboriginal languages is their language, and most of them are The Dreaming or Christian. Their strongholds are Moreton Commonwealth, Pilbara, Auralia. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

assamese.name: Assamese and Northeast peoples
assamese.note: Brahmaputra valley and the north-eastern hills
assamese.strong: Ganga Delta Commonwealth, Sagaing, Kachin State
assamese.desc: The Assamese and Northeast peoples are the people of the Brahmaputra valley and the north-eastern hills, and in 2240 they number about 24 million. Their valley has been a meeting place of Indian and Himalayan peoples for thousands of years. Assamese is their language, and most of them are Hindu or Christian. They are strongest in Ganga Delta Commonwealth, Sagaing, Kachin State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

chewa.name: Chewa, Bemba and Zambezi peoples
chewa.desc: The Chewa, Bemba and Zambezi peoples are the people of Malawi, Zambia, and in 2240 they number about 24 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Chichewa, Bemba, and most are Christian. Their strongholds are Tete, Zambezi Commonwealth, Katanga. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_afrolatino.name: Floridian Exiles
f_afrolatino.note: Caribbean Hispanic and African American families resettled in Georgia from drowned Florida
f_afrolatino.parents: Dominicans and Puerto Ricans + African Americans
f_afrolatino.language: Caribbean Spanish and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_afrolatino.faith: Catholic and Protestant (Black churches) families; many secular
f_afrolatino.desc: In Muskogee Sector, Dominicans and Puerto Ricans and African Americans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Floridian Exiles. At home they speak Caribbean Spanish and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Catholic or Protestant (Black churches) by family, and many are secular. They number about 24 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Muskogee Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

cree_ojibwe.name: Cree and Ojibwe
cree_ojibwe.note: Hudson Bay lowlands, Great Lakes north
cree_ojibwe.strong: Upper Canada, Superior Sector, Ottawa Crown District
cree_ojibwe.desc: In the Hudson Bay lowlands, Great Lakes north live the Cree and Ojibwe, a people of about 24 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Cree. In faith most are Midewiwin or Christian. Their strongholds are Upper Canada, Superior Sector, Ottawa Crown District. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

turkmen.name: Turkmens
turkmen.strong: Razavi Khorasan, Alborz Commonwealth, Yazd-Isfahan Satrapy
turkmen.desc: The Turkmens are the people of Turkmenistan, and in 2240 they number about 23 million. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Their language is Turkmen. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Razavi Khorasan, Alborz Commonwealth, Yazd-Isfahan Satrapy. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

quechua.name: Quechua
quechua.strong: Beni March, Lima Commonwealth, Amazonas-Caqueta Department
quechua.desc: The Quechua are the people of High Andes, and in 2240 they number about 23 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Quechua is their language, and most of them are Catholic with Andean tradition. They are strongest in Beni March, Lima Commonwealth, Amazonas-Caqueta Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

swahili.name: Swahili and coastal Bantu
swahili.desc: The people of the Tanzania, Kenya coast are the Swahili and coastal Bantu, about 23 million strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Swahili, and most are Muslim (coast) or Christian (inland). They are strongest in Morogoro-Lindi, Rift Valley Commonwealth, Manyara-Singida. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

javanese.name: Javanese
javanese.strong: East Java, Java Commonwealth, South Sumatra
javanese.desc: The people of Central and East Java are the Javanese, about 22 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Javanese, Indonesian, and most are Sunni Muslim or Kejawen. They are strongest in East Java, Java Commonwealth, South Sumatra. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_calimex.name: Sierra Calimex
f_calimex.note: Mexican and Anglo valley Californians moved inland from the coast
f_calimex.faith: Catholic and Protestant families; many secular
f_calimex.desc: The Sierra Calimex are a fusion people of 2240 from Las Californias Sector: Mexican and Anglo valley Californians moved inland from the coast, grown into one community. At home they speak American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Catholic or Protestant by family, and many are secular. About 21 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Las Californias Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

tibetan.name: Tibetans
tibetan.strong: Ganga Delta Commonwealth, West Bengal, Tianshan Commonwealth
tibetan.desc: The people of the Tibetan plateau are the Tibetans, about 21 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Tibetan is their language, and most of them are Tibetan Buddhist or Bon. Their strongholds are Ganga Delta Commonwealth, West Bengal, Tianshan Commonwealth. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

sakha.name: Sakha (Yakuts)
sakha.desc: The people of the Lena basin are the Sakha (Yakuts), about 21 million strong in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Their language is Sakha (Yakut), Russian. In faith most are Aar Aiyy (Sakha faith) or Orthodox. Their strongholds are Olonkho, Zeya, Amur Commonwealth. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

haitian.name: Haitians
haitian.desc: The Haitians are the people of Haiti, and in 2240 they number about 20 million. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Haitian Kreyòl is their language, and most of them are Catholic or Vodou. Their strongholds are Havana League Seat. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

scots.name: Scots
scots.desc: The Scots are the people of Scotland, and in 2240 they number about 20 million. They are heirs of the Celtic peoples who once held most of western Europe and who held on longest at its Atlantic edge. English is their language, and most of them are Secular or Presbyterian. Their strongholds are Highland, North Yorkshire. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

guarani.name: Paraguayans and Guaraní
guarani.strong: Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy, Sao Paulo Captaincy
guarani.desc: The Paraguayans and Guaraní are the people of Paraguay, and in 2240 they number about 20 million. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Guarani is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy, Sao Paulo Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_strait.name: Tsushima Strait Folk
f_strait.note: Korean and Japanese Busan-Fukuoka twin cities
f_strait.faith: Secular and Shinto and Buddhist families; many secular
f_strait.desc: In Han River Commonwealth, Koreans and Japanese families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Tsushima Strait Folk. At home they speak Korean and Japanese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Shinto or Buddhist by family, and many are secular. About 20 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Han River Commonwealth, Hiroshima Prefecture. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

afrikaner.name: Afrikaners and Cape coloureds
afrikaner.strong: Northern Cape, Free State, Eastern Cape
afrikaner.desc: The Afrikaners and Cape coloureds are the people of Western and Northern Cape, and in 2240 they number about 20 million. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Afrikaans is their language, and most of them are Reformed Christian. Their strongholds are Northern Cape, Free State, Eastern Cape. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

niger_delta.name: Niger Delta and Middle Belt peoples
niger_delta.strong: Abuja Federal Territory, Bauchi State, North
niger_delta.desc: The Niger Delta and Middle Belt peoples are the people of the Middle Belt, and in 2240 they number about 19 million. They belong to the Benue-Congo peoples of Nigeria's Middle Belt and Cross River, the cradle from which the Bantu once set out. Their language is Tiv. In faith most are Christian or Muslim. They are strongest in Abuja Federal Territory, Bauchi State, North. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_sertao.name: Sertão Solar Nordestinos
f_sertao.faith: Catholic and Candomblé families; many secular
f_sertao.strong: Pernambuco Captaincy, Ceara Captaincy, Bahia Captaincy
f_sertao.desc: The Sertão Solar Nordestinos are a fusion people of 2240 from Pernambuco Captaincy: Brazilian and Afro-Brazilian solar-farm backlands, grown into one community. At home they speak Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Catholic or Candomblé by family, and many are secular. About 19 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Pernambuco Captaincy, Ceara Captaincy, Bahia Captaincy. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

cuban.name: Cubans
cuban.desc: The Cubans are the people of Cuba, and in 2240 they number about 19 million. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Cuban Spanish. In faith most are Catholic or Santería. Their strongholds are Havana League Seat. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

amazigh.name: Amazigh (Berbers)
amazigh.strong: Tindouf Wilaya, Algiers Commonwealth, Ouargla Wilaya
amazigh.desc: The people of Atlas and Kabylie are the Amazigh (Berbers), about 18 million strong in 2240. They are the indigenous people of North Africa, older on their land than every empire that came to rule it. Tamazight is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Tindouf Wilaya, Algiers Commonwealth, Ouargla Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

evenk.name: Evenks and Evens
evenk.desc: The people of the Central Siberian Plateau are the Evenks and Evens, about 18 million strong in 2240. They come from the Tungusic peoples of the far north-east, reindeer herders, hunters and, once, the founders of China's last dynasty. Evenki is their language, and most of them are Shamanist or Orthodox. Their strongholds are Yeniseia, Olonkho, Baikalia. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

akan.name: Akan
akan.desc: The Akan are the people of Ghana, Ivory Coast, Togo, and in 2240 they number about 18 million. They are a Kwa people of the West African forest, heirs of kingdoms built on gold, kola and trade. They speak Akan (Twi, Fante), and most are Christian or Akan faith. Their strongholds are Savanes-Zanzan, Northern-Brong-Ahafo, Northern. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

yemeni.name: Yemenis
yemeni.strong: Shabwah Emirate, Najran-'Asir Emirate, Hadhramaut Emirate
yemeni.desc: In the Yemeni highlands live the Yemenis, a people of about 18 million in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Their language is Yemeni Arabic. In faith most are Zaydi and Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Shabwah Emirate, Najran-'Asir Emirate, Hadhramaut Emirate. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

malagasy.name: Coastal Malagasy
malagasy.desc: The Coastal Malagasy are the people of Madagascar, and in 2240 they number about 18 million. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Malagasy. In faith most are Christian or ancestral faith. Their strongholds are Imerina Commonwealth, Reunion, Atsimo-Andrefana. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

somali.name: Somalis
somali.desc: The Somalis are the people of Horn of Africa, and in 2240 they number about 17 million. They are a Cushitic people of the Horn of Africa, herders and traders on one of the oldest routes between Africa and Arabia. They speak Somali, and most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Somaliland, Bay-Hiran, Shewa Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

inuit.name: Inuit and Arctic natives
inuit.desc: The Inuit and Arctic natives are the people of Arctic coasts, Greenland, Alaska, and in 2240 they number about 17 million. They are the Arctic people who mastered the ice, hunting seal and whale from Greenland to Alaska. Their language is Inuktitut. In faith most are Christian or Inuit tradition. They are strongest in Ottawa Crown District, Vinland, Keewatin. The thaw opened the north of their land to farming, and new towns grew where there had been permafrost.

gan.name: Gan Chinese
gan.strong: Jiangxi Circuit, Yangtze Commonwealth, Fujian Circuit
gan.desc: The people of Jiangxi are the Gan Chinese, about 17 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. Their language is Gan Chinese. In faith most are Folk religion or Buddhist. Their strongholds are Jiangxi Circuit, Yangtze Commonwealth, Fujian Circuit. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_appalachian.name: Appalachian Highlanders
f_appalachian.language: English and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_appalachian.faith: Secular and Protestant families; many secular
f_appalachian.desc: In Westsylvania Sector, Scots and Anglo-Americans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Appalachian Highlanders. At home they speak English and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Protestant by family, and many are secular. They number about 17 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Westsylvania Sector, Franklin Sector. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_amurese.name: Amurese
f_amurese.note: Russian and Northern Han families of the Amur boom towns
f_amurese.faith: Orthodox Christian and Secular families; many secular
f_amurese.strong: Harbin Capital District, Amur Commonwealth, Zeya
f_amurese.desc: In Harbin Capital District, Russians and Northern Han families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Amurese. Their everyday speech mixes Russian and Mandarin. In faith they are Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 17 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Harbin Capital District, Amur Commonwealth, Zeya. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

pahari.name: Paharis (Garhwali, Kumaoni, Himachali)
pahari.desc: In Western Himalaya live the Paharis (Garhwali, Kumaoni, Himachali), a people of about 17 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Garhwali, Kumaoni, Himachali, and most are Hindu. They are strongest in Delhi Commonwealth, Himachal Pradesh. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

uyghur.name: Uyghurs
uyghur.desc: The Uyghurs are the people of the Tarim basin, and in 2240 they number about 16 million. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. They speak Uyghur, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Tianshan Commonwealth, Gorno-Badakhshan, Almaty. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

uzbek.name: Uzbeks
uzbek.note: Uzbekistan, Fergana; migrant towns across southern Siberia
uzbek.strong: Tashkent Capital District, Gorno-Badakhshan, Razavi Khorasan
uzbek.desc: The people of Uzbekistan, Fergana are the Uzbeks, about 16 million strong in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. They speak Uzbek, and most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Tashkent Capital District, Gorno-Badakhshan, Razavi Khorasan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

oromo.name: Oromo
oromo.desc: The people of Southern and central Ethiopia are the Oromo, about 16 million strong in 2240. They are a Cushitic people of the Horn of Africa, herders and traders on one of the oldest routes between Africa and Arabia. Their language is Oromo. In faith most are Muslim, Christian or Waaqeffanna. Their strongholds are Shewa Commonwealth, Amhara, Jonglei. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

bedouin.name: Bedouin
bedouin.strong: Damascus Capital District, Al Madinah Emirate, Al-Jowf-Tabuk Emirate
bedouin.desc: The Bedouin are the people of the Nafud, Syrian desert, Sinai interior, and in 2240 they number about 16 million. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Bedouin Arabic, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Damascus Capital District, Al Madinah Emirate, Al-Jowf-Tabuk Emirate. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

bulgarian.name: Bulgarians and Macedonians
bulgarian.strong: Attic Commonwealth, East Macedonia and Thrace, Wallachian Commonwealth
bulgarian.desc: In Eastern Balkans live the Bulgarians and Macedonians, a people of about 16 million in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. They speak Bulgarian, Macedonian, and most are Orthodox Christian. Their strongholds are Attic Commonwealth, East Macedonia and Thrace, Wallachian Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

romanian.name: Romanians and Moldovans
romanian.strong: Wallachian Commonwealth, East Macedonia and Thrace, Belgrade Federal District
romanian.desc: The people of Danube and Carpathians are the Romanians and Moldovans, about 15 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Romanian. In faith most are Orthodox Christian. They are strongest in Wallachian Commonwealth, East Macedonia and Thrace, Belgrade Federal District. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

iraqi.name: Mesopotamian Arabs
iraqi.note: Tigris and Euphrates; much of the old delta under the sea
iraqi.strong: Two Rivers Commonwealth, Lorestan-Khuzestan Satrapy, East Azerbaijan
iraqi.desc: The Mesopotamian Arabs are the people of Tigris and Euphrates, and in 2240 they number about 15 million. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Mesopotamian Arabic, and most are Shia and Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Two Rivers Commonwealth, Lorestan-Khuzestan Satrapy, East Azerbaijan. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

portuguese.name: Portuguese
portuguese.desc: The people of Portugal are the Portuguese, about 15 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Portuguese is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Caceres-Badajoz, Castilian Commonwealth, Azores. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

mongo.name: Mongo and forest peoples
mongo.desc: The people of the Central Congo basin are the Mongo and forest peoples, about 15 million strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Lomongo. In faith most are Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Pool Commonwealth, Kasai-Oriental, Equateur. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

hakka.name: Hakka
hakka.note: Hakka hills of Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi
hakka.desc: In Hakka hills of Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi live the Hakka, a people of about 15 million in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. They speak Hakka, and most are Folk religion or Christian. They are strongest in Pearl River Commonwealth, Fujian Circuit. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

omani.name: Omanis
omani.strong: Al Wusta Emirate, Al Batinah North Satrapy, Dhofar Emirate
omani.desc: The people of Hajar mountains, Dhofar are the Omanis, about 15 million strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Omani Arabic is their language, and most of them are Ibadi Muslim. Their strongholds are Al Wusta Emirate, Al Batinah North Satrapy, Dhofar Emirate. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_koreohan.name: Liaodong Koreo-Han
f_koreohan.note: Korean and Han Manchurian industrial cities
f_koreohan.desc: The people of Liaoning Circuit are the Liaodong Koreo-Han, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Koreans and Northern Han families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Korean and Mandarin. In faith they are mostly secular. About 14 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Liaoning Circuit, Jilin Circuit. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

burman.name: Bamar (Burmese)
burman.desc: The people of the Irrawaddy dry zone are the Bamar (Burmese), about 14 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Burmese. In faith most are Theravada Buddhist. They are strongest in Shan State, Sagaing, Kachin State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

fang.name: Fang and Cameroon peoples
fang.desc: The Fang and Cameroon peoples are the people of Cameroon, Gabon, and in 2240 they number about 14 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Fang, Beti, French, and most are Christian or Bwiti. Their strongholds are East-Centre, Likouala-Sangha, North. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

great_lakes.name: Great Lakes Bantu
great_lakes.strong: North Kivu, Rift Valley Commonwealth, Orientale
great_lakes.desc: The Great Lakes Bantu are the people of Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and in 2240 they number about 13 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Kinyarwanda is their language, and most of them are Christian. Their strongholds are North Kivu, Rift Valley Commonwealth, Orientale. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

ovimbundu.name: Ovimbundu and Angolans
ovimbundu.desc: In the Angolan plateau live the Ovimbundu and Angolans, a people of about 13 million in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Umbundu is their language, and most of them are Christian. They are strongest in Malanje-Bie, Huila-Namibe, Cuando Cubango. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_fujian.name: Fujian Strait Austronesians
f_fujian.note: Min and Filipino seafarers of the strait
f_fujian.parents: Min Chinese + Tagalog and Luzon peoples
f_fujian.faith: Folk religion (Mazu) and Roman Catholic families; many secular
