f_fujian.desc: The people of Fujian Circuit are the Fujian Strait Austronesians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Min Chinese and Tagalog and Luzon peoples families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Hokkien and Tagalog. In faith they are Folk religion (Mazu) or Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 13 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Fujian Circuit. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

czech.name: Czechs
czech.strong: Banska Bystrica March, Bavaria Kreis, Central Bohemian March
czech.desc: In Bohemia, Moravia live the Czechs, a people of about 13 million in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Czech is their language, and most of them are Largely secular or Catholic minority. Their strongholds are Banska Bystrica March, Bavaria Kreis, Central Bohemian March. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_sinojava.name: Bogor Sino-Javanese
f_sinojava.note: Javanese and Han hill city above drowned Jakarta
f_sinojava.faith: Sunni Muslim and Secular families; many secular
f_sinojava.desc: The Bogor Sino-Javanese are a fusion people of 2240 from Java Commonwealth: Javanese and Han hill city above drowned Jakarta, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Javanese and Mandarin. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 13 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Java Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

tajik.name: Tajiks
tajik.strong: Indus Capital Territory, Gorno-Badakhshan, Razavi Khorasan
tajik.desc: The Tajiks are the people of Tajikistan, and in 2240 they number about 13 million. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. Their language is Tajik Persian. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Indus Capital Territory, Gorno-Badakhshan, Razavi Khorasan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

zhuang.name: Zhuang
zhuang.strong: Guangxi Circuit, Guizhou Circuit, Pearl River Commonwealth
zhuang.desc: In Guangxi live the Zhuang, a people of about 12 million in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. Their language is Zhuang. In faith most are Mo folk religion or Buddhist. They are strongest in Guangxi Circuit, Guizhou Circuit, Pearl River Commonwealth. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

malayali.name: Malayalis
malayali.note: Kerala; a large presence in the inland Gulf
malayali.strong: Tamil Nadu, Najd Commonwealth, Eastern Emirate
malayali.desc: The people of Kerala are the Malayalis, about 12 million strong in 2240. Their Dravidian language is older in India than the Indo-Aryan ones, with a literature reaching back two thousand years. Their language is Malayalam. In faith most are Hindu, Muslim or Christian. They are strongest in Tamil Nadu, Najd Commonwealth, Eastern Emirate. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

azerbaijani.name: Azerbaijanis
azerbaijani.desc: In Azerbaijan, Iranian Azerbaijan live the Azerbaijanis, a people of about 12 million in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. They speak Azerbaijani, and most are Shia Muslim or secular. They are strongest in Kura Commonwealth, East Azerbaijan, Daghestan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

saraiki.name: Saraikis
saraiki.desc: The people of Southern Punjab are the Saraikis, about 12 million strong in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Saraiki is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Ravi Commonwealth, Balochistan March. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

zapotec.name: Zapotec and Mixtec
zapotec.desc: The Zapotec and Mixtec are the people of Oaxaca, and in 2240 they number about 12 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Zapotec is their language, and most of them are Catholic. Their strongholds are Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

nilotic.name: Nilotic peoples
nilotic.strong: Rift Valley Commonwealth, Shewa Commonwealth, Western Bahr el Ghazal Nome
nilotic.desc: The people of South Sudan, Kenyan rift, Karamoja are the Nilotic peoples, about 12 million strong in 2240. They are a Nilotic people, cattle herders of the Nile and the Rift, tall, proud and stubborn about their land. They speak Dinka, Nuer, Luo, Kalenjin, and most are Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Rift Valley Commonwealth, Shewa Commonwealth, Western Bahr el Ghazal Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

xiang.name: Xiang Chinese
xiang.strong: Hunan Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit, Guangxi Circuit
xiang.desc: The Xiang Chinese are the people of Hunan, and in 2240 they number about 11 million. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. They speak Xiang Chinese, and most are Folk religion or secular. Their strongholds are Hunan Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit, Guangxi Circuit. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_hudson.name: Hudson Highland Polyglots
f_hudson.note: Caribbean and Jewish New Yorkers resettled up-river after the flood
f_hudson.language: Caribbean Spanish and Hebrew (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_hudson.faith: Catholic and Judaism families; many secular
f_hudson.desc: The people of Columbia Commonwealth are the Hudson Highland Polyglots, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Dominicans and Puerto Ricans and Israelis families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Caribbean Spanish and Hebrew. In faith they are Catholic or Judaism by family, and many are secular. They number about 11 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Columbia Commonwealth, New England Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

belarusian.name: Belarusians
belarusian.strong: Minsk-Gomel, Muscovy Commonwealth, Riga Hanse District
belarusian.desc: The people of Belarus are the Belarusians, about 11 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Their language is Belarusian. In faith most are Orthodox Christian. Their strongholds are Minsk-Gomel, Muscovy Commonwealth, Riga Hanse District. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

shona.name: Shona
shona.desc: In Zimbabwe live the Shona, a people of about 11 million in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Shona, and most are Christian or ancestral faith. Their strongholds are Tete, Zambezi Commonwealth, Manica-Gaza. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

welsh.name: Welsh
welsh.desc: In Wales live the Welsh, a people of about 10 million in 2240. They are heirs of the Celtic peoples who once held most of western Europe and who held on longest at its Atlantic edge. They speak Welsh, English, and most are Nonconformist heritage or secular. They are strongest in Home Counties Commonwealth, North Yorkshire. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_pearl.name: Pearl Delta Neo-Cantonese
f_pearl.note: Cantonese and Filipino shipyard crews of the raised delta
f_pearl.faith: Folk religion and Roman Catholic families; many secular
f_pearl.desc: In Pearl River Commonwealth, Cantonese and Tagalog and Luzon peoples families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Pearl Delta Neo-Cantonese. At home they speak Cantonese and Tagalog, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Folk religion or Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 10 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Pearl River Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_delhi.name: Delhi Punjabi-Hindustanis
f_delhi.faith: Sikh and Hindu families; many secular
f_delhi.desc: The Delhi Punjabi-Hindustanis are a fusion people of 2240 from Delhi Commonwealth: Punjabi and Hindustani capital families, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Punjabi and Hindi-Urdu. In faith they are Sikh or Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 10 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Delhi Commonwealth, Uttar Pradesh. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_tejano.name: Tejano-Texians
f_tejano.note: Mexican and Anglo Texans of the hill-country cities
f_tejano.language: Mexican Spanish and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_tejano.faith: Roman Catholic and Protestant families; many secular
f_tejano.desc: In Tejas Sector, Mexicans and Anglo-Americans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Tejano-Texians. At home they speak Mexican Spanish and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Protestant by family, and many are secular. About 10 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Tejas Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

lao.name: Lao
lao.desc: The people of the Mekong north are the Lao, about 10 million strong in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. Lao is their language, and most of them are Theravada Buddhist. They are strongest in Luang Prabang, Vientiane-Savannakhet, Gia Lai. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_nikkei.name: Cascadian Nikkei-Yankees
f_nikkei.note: Japanese and Anglo Pacific Northwest families
f_nikkei.language: Japanese and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_nikkei.faith: Shinto and Buddhist and Protestant families; many secular
f_nikkei.desc: The Cascadian Nikkei-Yankees are a fusion people of 2240 from Las Californias Sector: Japanese and Anglo Pacific Northwest families, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Japanese and American English. In faith they are Shinto or Buddhist or Protestant by family, and many are secular. They number about 9.6 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Las Californias Sector, Jefferson Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

kanuri.name: Kanuri and Chadians
kanuri.desc: The people of Lake Chad, Chad are the Kanuri and Chadians, about 9.5 million strong in 2240. They are a Saharan people, heirs of the trans-desert caravan kingdoms around Lake Chad. Kanuri is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Guera, Haute-Kotto Prefecture, North. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

baloch.name: Baloch
baloch.strong: Sindh March, Sistan and Baluchestan March, Balochistan March
baloch.desc: The Baloch are the people of Balochistan, and in 2240 they number about 9.5 million. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. They speak Balochi, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Sindh March, Sistan and Baluchestan March, Balochistan March. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

dutch.name: Dutch and Flemish
dutch.note: Low Countries, inland of the 2240 coast
dutch.strong: Hesse Kreis, Randstad Free Cities, Saone-et-Loire
dutch.desc: The people of Low Countries are the Dutch and Flemish, about 9.4 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak Dutch, and most are Secular or Catholic and Protestant. They are strongest in Hesse Kreis, Randstad Free Cities, Saone-et-Loire. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

miao.name: Miao and Hmong
miao.strong: Guizhou Circuit, Guangxi Circuit, Hunan Circuit
miao.desc: The people of Guizhou are the Miao and Hmong, about 9.3 million strong in 2240. They are a Hmong-Mien people of the southern Chinese mountains, long known for their embroidery, silver and independence. Their language is Hmong-Mien languages. In faith most are Animist or Christian. They are strongest in Guizhou Circuit, Guangxi Circuit, Hunan Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

santal.name: Santals
santal.note: Chota Nagpur and the Santal Parganas
santal.desc: The Santals are the people of Chota Nagpur and the Santal Parganas, and in 2240 they number about 9.2 million. They speak an Austroasiatic language, the tongue of the first rice farmers of mainland Southeast Asia. Santali is their language, and most of them are Sarna faith or Christian. Their strongholds are West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

bhil.name: Bhils
bhil.desc: The Bhils are the people of the Malwa and the Satpura hills, and in 2240 they number about 8.9 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Bhili, and most are Hindu or folk faith. They are strongest in Deccan Commonwealth, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

finnic.name: Finns and Karelians
finnic.desc: In Finland, Karelia live the Finns and Karelians, a people of about 8.6 million in 2240. Their Finnic tongue came west with Uralic-speaking hunters and farmers thousands of years ago and survived among the forests and lakes of the north. Finnish is their language, and most of them are Lutheran heritage or secular. They are strongest in North Karelia, Pirkanmaa, Muscovy Commonwealth. The warming made their northern lands milder and busier than ever, and ice-free seas opened new ports.

swiss_romansh.name: Swiss Alpine peoples
swiss_romansh.desc: The Swiss Alpine peoples are the people of Swiss and Tyrolean Alps, and in 2240 they number about 8.5 million. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Swiss German is their language, and most of them are Catholic and Reformed. They are strongest in Trentino-Turin, Baden-Wuerttemberg Kreis, Isere-Drome. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_jing.name: Jing Spaceport Kin
f_jing.note: Han and Russian families of the northern launch complexes
f_jing.faith: Secular and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_jing.strong: Zhili Commonwealth, Gansu Circuit, Inner Mongolia Aimag
f_jing.desc: In Zhili Commonwealth, Northern Han and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Jing Spaceport Kin. Their everyday speech mixes Mandarin and Russian. In faith they are Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 8.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Zhili Commonwealth, Gansu Circuit, Inner Mongolia Aimag. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_agrogaucho.name: Cerrado Agro-Gaúchos
f_agrogaucho.language: Rioplatense Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_agrogaucho.faith: Roman Catholic and Catholic families; many secular
f_agrogaucho.desc: In Planalto Federal District, Rioplatenses and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Cerrado Agro-Gaúchos. Their everyday speech mixes Rioplatense Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. In faith they are Roman Catholic or Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 7.9 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Planalto Federal District. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

khmer.name: Khmer
khmer.desc: The Khmer are the people of Cambodia, and in 2240 they number about 7.8 million. They speak an Austroasiatic language, the tongue of the first rice farmers of mainland Southeast Asia. Khmer is their language, and most of them are Theravada Buddhist. Their strongholds are Chao Phraya Commonwealth, Gia Lai. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

shan.name: Shan and hill peoples
shan.desc: In the Shan plateau, Kachin hills live the Shan and hill peoples, a people of about 7.7 million in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. They speak Shan, Kachin and hill languages, and most are Theravada Buddhist or Christian. They are strongest in Shan State, Yunnan Circuit, Sagaing. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

yi.name: Yi
yi.strong: Chengdu Commonwealth, Yunnan Circuit, Guizhou Circuit
yi.desc: The people of Liangshan are the Yi, about 7.7 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Nuosu (Yi) is their language, and most of them are Bimo faith. They are strongest in Chengdu Commonwealth, Yunnan Circuit, Guizhou Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

banda_zande.name: Banda, Gbaya and Zande
banda_zande.desc: In Central African Republic, Uele live the Banda, Gbaya and Zande, a people of about 7.7 million in 2240. They are the peoples of the Ubangi savannah, whose kingdoms long stood between the Sahel and the forest. Banda is their language, and most of them are Christian. Their strongholds are Haute-Kotto Prefecture, Equateur, East-Centre. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_hispanofil.name: Hispano-Filipinos
f_hispanofil.note: Filipino and Spanish Manila highland families
f_hispanofil.desc: The people of Maynila Commonwealth are the Hispano-Filipinos, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Tagalog and Luzon peoples and Spaniards families met and married. At home they speak Tagalog and Spanish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 7.7 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Maynila Commonwealth, Mait, Luzonia. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_bengaluru.name: Bengaluru Neo-Kannadigas
f_bengaluru.desc: The Bengaluru Neo-Kannadigas are a fusion people of 2240 from Tamil Nadu: Kannada and Tamil tech-plateau city, grown into one community. At home they speak Kannada and Tamil, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 7.7 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Tamil Nadu, Kaveri Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

guarani_ind.name: Guaraní peoples
guarani_ind.strong: Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Santa Cruz March, Boqueron March
guarani_ind.desc: In the Chaco and eastern Paraguay forests live the Guaraní peoples, a people of about 7.6 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Guarani is their language, and most of them are Guarani faith or Christian. They are strongest in Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Santa Cruz March, Boqueron March. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

haudenosaunee.name: Haudenosaunee
haudenosaunee.language: Mohawk, Seneca and other Iroquoian languages
haudenosaunee.desc: The Haudenosaunee are the people of Upstate New York and Ontario, and in 2240 they number about 7.6 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Mohawk is their language, and most of them are Longhouse or Christian. Their strongholds are Columbia Commonwealth. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

catalan.name: Catalans
catalan.desc: The people of Catalonia, Valencia, Balearics are the Catalans, about 7.4 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Catalan. In faith most are Secular or Catholic heritage. Their strongholds are Zaragoza-Teruel, Dordogne-Aveyron. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_osaka.name: Kansai Neo-Zainichi
f_osaka.faith: Shinto and Buddhist and Secular families; many secular
f_osaka.desc: In Kanto Commonwealth, Japanese and Koreans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Kansai Neo-Zainichi. At home they speak Japanese and Korean, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Shinto or Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 7.4 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Kanto Commonwealth. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_cdmx.name: Anahuac Orbital Mestizos
f_cdmx.note: Mexican and Nahua capital and launch-valley families
f_cdmx.language: Mexican Spanish and Nahuatl (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_cdmx.faith: Roman Catholic and Catholic with Mesoamerican tradition families; many secular
f_cdmx.desc: The people of Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth are the Anahuac Orbital Mestizos, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Mexicans and Maya and Nahua peoples families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Mexican Spanish and Nahuatl. In faith they are Roman Catholic or Catholic with Mesoamerican tradition by family, and many are secular. They number about 7.2 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

georgian.name: Georgians
georgian.desc: The Georgians are the people of Georgia, and in 2240 they number about 7.2 million. Their Kartvelian language and alphabet are unique to the Caucasus, and their kingdom was among the first to adopt Christianity. Georgian is their language, and most of them are Georgian Orthodox. They are strongest in Kura Commonwealth, Daghestan, Kuban Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_rainbow.name: Highveld Rainbow Synthesis
f_rainbow.parents: Zulu and Nguni + Afrikaners and Cape coloureds
f_rainbow.faith: Christian and Reformed Christian families; many secular
f_rainbow.desc: The people of Highveld Commonwealth are the Highveld Rainbow Synthesis, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Zulu and Nguni and Afrikaners and Cape coloureds families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes isiZulu and Afrikaans. In faith they are Christian or Reformed Christian by family, and many are secular. About 7.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Highveld Commonwealth, Free State, Limpopo. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_wuhan.name: Wuhan Riverine Hybrids
f_wuhan.note: Wu and Xiang Yangtze river-port people
f_wuhan.language: Wu (Shanghainese) and Xiang Chinese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_wuhan.faith: Secular and Folk religion families; many secular
f_wuhan.strong: Yangtze Commonwealth, Hubei Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit
f_wuhan.desc: The people of Yangtze Commonwealth are the Wuhan Riverine Hybrids, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Wu Chinese and Xiang Chinese families met and married. At home they speak Wu, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Folk religion by family, and many are secular. About 7.0 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Yangtze Commonwealth, Hubei Circuit, Jiangxi Circuit. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

mossi.name: Mossi and Voltaic peoples
mossi.desc: The people of Burkina Faso are the Mossi and Voltaic peoples, about 6.9 million strong in 2240. They are a Gur-speaking people of the West African savannah, farmers whose chiefdoms resisted the great empires around them. Their language is Moore. In faith most are Muslim, Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Northern-Brong-Ahafo, Mopti, Niger Bend Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_nipopaulista.name: Nipo-Paulistas
f_nipopaulista.note: Japanese and Brazilian São Paulo highlanders
f_nipopaulista.language: Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_nipopaulista.faith: Shinto and Buddhist and Catholic families; many secular
f_nipopaulista.desc: In Sao Paulo Captaincy, Japanese and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Nipo-Paulistas. At home they speak Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Shinto or Buddhist or Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 6.8 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Sao Paulo Captaincy. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_mineiro.name: Afro-Mineiros
f_mineiro.note: Afro-Brazilian and Portuguese Minas mining towns
f_mineiro.language: Brazilian Portuguese and Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_mineiro.faith: Candomblé and Roman Catholic families; many secular
f_mineiro.desc: The people of Minas Gerais Captaincy are the Afro-Mineiros, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Afro-Brazilians and Portuguese families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Brazilian Portuguese and Portuguese. In faith they are Candomblé or Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 6.7 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Minas Gerais Captaincy. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

acehnese.name: Acehnese
acehnese.desc: The people of Aceh are the Acehnese, about 6.6 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Acehnese. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Deli Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

armenian.name: Armenians
armenian.desc: In Armenia live the Armenians, a people of about 6.5 million in 2240. Their nation is one of the oldest in the world: the first to make Christianity a state faith, scattered by catastrophe and never dissolved. They speak Armenian, and most are Armenian Apostolic. They are strongest in Kura Commonwealth, East Azerbaijan, Erzurum-Diyarbakir. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

kikuyu.name: Kikuyu and Kenyan highlanders
kikuyu.desc: In the Central Kenya, Lake Victoria shore live the Kikuyu and Kenyan highlanders, a people of about 6.3 million in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Kikuyu, Swahili, English, and most are Christian. They are strongest in Rift Valley Commonwealth, Coast, Manyara-Singida. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

yao_mien.name: Yao (Mien)
yao_mien.desc: The Yao (Mien) are the people of the Nanling mountains, and in 2240 they number about 6.2 million. They are a Hmong-Mien people of the southern Chinese mountains, long known for their embroidery, silver and independence. Their language is Iu Mien. In faith most are Taoist folk religion. They are strongest in Pearl River Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

afro_colombian.name: Afro-Colombians
afro_colombian.strong: Bogota Capital District, Canal Free Zone
afro_colombian.desc: The Afro-Colombians are the people of the Pacific Chocó and Caribbean coast, and in 2240 they number about 6.2 million. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. They speak Colombian Spanish, Palenquero, and most are Catholic. They are strongest in Bogota Capital District, Canal Free Zone. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_mumbai.name: Ghats Bollywood Creoles
f_mumbai.note: Marathi and Gujarati film-and-finance city on the Ghats
f_mumbai.desc: The people of Deccan Commonwealth are the Ghats Bollywood Creoles, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Marathis and Gujaratis families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Marathi and Gujarati. In faith they are Hindu by family, and many are secular. They number about 6.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Deccan Commonwealth. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

ngalop.name: Bhutanese (Ngalop)
ngalop.desc: The people of Bhutan are the Bhutanese (Ngalop), about 6.1 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Dzongkha. In faith most are Drukpa Kagyu Buddhist. They are strongest in West Bengal. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_navhispano.name: Plateau Navajo-Hispanos
f_navhispano.language: Diné bizaad and Mexican Spanish (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_navhispano.faith: Diné tradition and Roman Catholic families; many secular
f_navhispano.desc: In Tejas Sector, Navajo and Pueblo peoples and Mexicans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Plateau Navajo-Hispanos. Their everyday speech mixes Diné bizaad and Mexican Spanish. In faith they are Diné tradition or Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.8 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Tejas Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

manchu.name: Manchu
manchu.strong: Liaoning Circuit, Jilin Circuit, South Hamgyong Province
manchu.desc: In Hills of Liaoning and Jilin live the Manchu, a people of about 5.8 million in 2240. They come from the Tungusic peoples of the far north-east, reindeer herders, hunters and, once, the founders of China's last dynasty. Their language is Mandarin. In faith most are Folk religion or shamanist. They are strongest in Liaoning Circuit, Jilin Circuit, South Hamgyong Province. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

jamaican.name: Jamaicans
jamaican.desc: The people of Jamaica are the Jamaicans, about 5.8 million strong in 2240. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Their language is Jamaican Patois. In faith most are Protestant or Rastafari. They are strongest in Havana League Seat. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_deccani.name: Hyderabad Deccanis
f_deccani.desc: The Hyderabad Deccanis are a fusion people of 2240 from Telangana: Telugu and Hindustani Deccan city, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Telugu and Hindi-Urdu. In faith they are Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 5.5 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Telangana. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_baydesi.name: Bay Silicon Desi
f_baydesi.note: Indian and Anglo engineers of the inland Bay
f_baydesi.language: Hindi-Urdu and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_baydesi.faith: Hindu and Protestant families; many secular
f_baydesi.desc: The Bay Silicon Desi are a fusion people of 2240 from Las Californias Sector: Indian and Anglo engineers of the inland Bay, grown into one community. At home they speak Hindi-Urdu and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Hindu or Protestant by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.5 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Las Californias Sector. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_afrogaul.name: Paris Afro-Gauls
f_afrogaul.faith: Secular and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_afrogaul.desc: The Paris Afro-Gauls are a fusion people of 2240 from Ile-de-France Commonwealth: French and Mande Parisians, grown into one community. At home they speak French and Bambara, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.4 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Ile-de-France Commonwealth, Saone-et-Loire. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_pudong.name: Pudong Arcologists
f_pudong.note: Wu and Japanese engineers of the stilt arcologies over drowned Shanghai
f_pudong.faith: Secular and Shinto and Buddhist families; many secular
f_pudong.desc: The people of Yangtze Commonwealth are the Pudong Arcologists, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Wu Chinese and Japanese families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Wu. In faith they are Shinto or Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Yangtze Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_moskavkaz.name: Moscow Caucasian-Rus
f_moskavkaz.note: North Caucasian and Russian capital families
f_moskavkaz.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_moskavkaz.desc: The Moscow Caucasian-Rus are a fusion people of 2240 from Muscovy Commonwealth: North Caucasian and Russian capital families, grown into one community. At home they speak Adyghe and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Muscovy Commonwealth. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_steppehan.name: Inner Mongol Steppe Han
f_steppehan.note: Mongol and Han wind-farm steppe towns
f_steppehan.faith: Tibetan Buddhist and Secular families; many secular
f_steppehan.strong: Shanxi Circuit, Inner Mongolia Aimag, Shaanxi Circuit
f_steppehan.desc: The Inner Mongol Steppe Han are a fusion people of 2240 from Shanxi Circuit: Mongol and Han wind-farm steppe towns, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Mongolian and Mandarin. In faith they are Tibetan Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 5.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Shanxi Circuit, Inner Mongolia Aimag, Shaanxi Circuit. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

gond.name: Adivasi peoples
gond.desc: In the Central Indian hills live the Adivasi peoples, a people of about 5.1 million in 2240. They are among the oldest peoples of India, keeping their own gods, councils and forests through every empire. They speak Gondi, Kurukh, Ho and others, and most are Folk faiths or Hindu. Their strongholds are Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

hungarian.name: Hungarians
hungarian.strong: Banska Bystrica March, Alba-Bihor, Banja Luka
hungarian.desc: The people of the Pannonian basin are the Hungarians, about 5.1 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors rode west from the Urals in the ninth century and settled the Carpathian basin for good. They speak Hungarian, and most are Catholic and Reformed. Their strongholds are Banska Bystrica March, Alba-Bihor, Banja Luka. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_italopaulista.name: Italo-Paulistas
f_italopaulista.note: Italian and Brazilian interior São Paulo
f_italopaulista.language: Italian and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_italopaulista.faith: Roman Catholic and Catholic families; many secular
f_italopaulista.desc: The people of Sao Paulo Captaincy are the Italo-Paulistas, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Italians and Brazilians families met and married. At home they speak Italian and Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 5.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Sao Paulo Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

tujia.name: Tujia
tujia.strong: Chongqing Circuit, Hubei Circuit, Hunan Circuit
tujia.desc: The people of the Wuling mountains are the Tujia, about 5.1 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. They speak Tujia, Mandarin, and most are Folk religion. They are strongest in Chongqing Circuit, Hubei Circuit, Hunan Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

occitan.name: Occitans
occitan.desc: The people of Languedoc, Provence, Gascony are the Occitans, about 5.0 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. They speak Occitan, French, and most are Secular or Catholic heritage. Their strongholds are Zaragoza-Teruel, Dordogne-Aveyron. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

bhojpuri.name: Bhojpuris
bhojpuri.desc: The Bhojpuris are the people of Eastern Uttar Pradesh, and in 2240 they number about 5.0 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Bhojpuri is their language, and most of them are Hindu or Muslim. Their strongholds are Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnali Zone. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

ob_exiles.name: Ob Sea exiles
ob_exiles.note: Families of the drowned West Siberian lowland, resettled on the Altai and Kuznetsk uplands
ob_exiles.desc: The Ob Sea exiles are the people of Kuznetsk, and in 2240 they number about 5.0 million. Siberian Russian is their language, and most of them are Orthodox or secular. They are strongest in Kuznetsk, Oirotia II, Ob Commonwealth. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

merina.name: Merina and Highland Malagasy
merina.desc: The people of the Malagasy highlands are the Merina and Highland Malagasy, about 5.0 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Malagasy (Merina), and most are Christian or Famadihana. Their strongholds are Imerina Commonwealth, Atsimo-Andrefana, Sofia-Toamasina. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

afro_carib.name: Lesser Antilleans and Bahamians
afro_carib.desc: In Lesser Antilles, Bahamas live the Lesser Antilleans and Bahamians, a people of about 5.0 million in 2240. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Their language is English creoles. In faith most are Christian or Vodou. They are strongest in Martinique-Guadeloupe, Guarico Department, Bolivar Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

walloon.name: Walloons
walloon.strong: Randstad Free Cities, Hesse Kreis, Saone-et-Loire
walloon.desc: The people of Wallonia are the Walloons, about 4.9 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. French is their language, and most of them are Catholic or secular. They are strongest in Randstad Free Cities, Hesse Kreis, Saone-et-Loire. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

navajo.name: Navajo and Pueblo peoples
navajo.desc: The Navajo and Pueblo peoples are the people of the Colorado plateau, and in 2240 they number about 4.9 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Diné bizaad. In faith most are Diné tradition or Christian. They are strongest in Deseret Sector. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

naga.name: Nagas
naga.desc: The Nagas are the people of the Naga hills, and in 2240 they number about 4.7 million. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Naga languages. In faith most are Baptist Christian. Their strongholds are Ganga Delta Commonwealth. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

xhosa.name: Xhosa
xhosa.strong: Eastern Cape, Free State, Northern Cape
xhosa.desc: The Xhosa are the people of Eastern Cape, and in 2240 they number about 4.6 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. isiXhosa is their language, and most of them are Christian or ancestral faith. They are strongest in Eastern Cape, Free State, Northern Cape. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_bogota.name: Bogotá Andean-Caribbeans
f_bogota.parents: Colombians and Venezuelans + Lesser Antilleans and Bahamians
f_bogota.language: Colombian and Venezuelan Spanish and English creoles (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_bogota.faith: Roman Catholic and Christian families; many secular
f_bogota.desc: The people of Bogota Capital District are the Bogotá Andean-Caribbeans, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Colombians and Venezuelans and Lesser Antilleans and Bahamians families met and married. At home they speak Colombian and Venezuelan Spanish and English creoles, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 4.6 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Bogota Capital District. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

kyrgyz.name: Kyrgyz
kyrgyz.desc: The people of Tian Shan are the Kyrgyz, about 4.6 million strong in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. They speak Kyrgyz, and most are Sunni Muslim or Tengrist revival. They are strongest in Almaty, Tashkent Capital District. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

pa_dutch.name: Pennsylvania Dutch
pa_dutch.desc: The people of South-central Pennsylvania are the Pennsylvania Dutch, about 4.5 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak Pennsylvania German, English, and most are Amish and Mennonite. They are strongest in Columbia Commonwealth. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

austral.name: Austral settlers (Antarctic)
austral.note: Antarctic Trust settlers: Chilean, Argentine, Australian, New Zealand, South African and Chinese roots
austral.strong: Palmer Land Trust Zone, Wilkes Land Trust Zone, Victoria Land Trust Zone
austral.desc: In Palmer Land Trust Zone live the Austral settlers (Antarctic), a people of about 4.5 million in 2240. They speak Antarctic English-Spanish contact speech, and most are Secular. They are strongest in Palmer Land Trust Zone, Wilkes Land Trust Zone, Victoria Land Trust Zone. They live on the newest settled land on Earth, the ice-free coasts of Antarctica, under the Antarctic Trust.

tuareg.name: Tuareg
tuareg.desc: In Central Sahara live the Tuareg, a people of about 4.5 million in 2240. They are the indigenous people of North Africa, older on their land than every empire that came to rule it. Their language is Tamasheq. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Ouargla Wilaya, Tahoua-Tillaberi, Illizi Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

igbo.name: Igbo
igbo.desc: In South-east Nigeria live the Igbo, a people of about 4.4 million in 2240. Their forebears built the forest kingdoms and city-states of the lower Niger, famous for bronze, trade and art. Their language is Igbo. In faith most are Christian or Odinani. They are strongest in Abuja Federal Territory. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

otomi_totonac.name: Otomí and Totonac
otomi_totonac.desc: The Otomí and Totonac are the people of the Hidalgo and Veracruz highlands, and in 2240 they number about 4.3 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Otomí. In faith most are Catholic with Native tradition. Their strongholds are Valley of Anahuac Commonwealth. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_anglodesi.name: London Anglo-Desi
f_anglodesi.note: English and Punjabi Londoners on the higher boroughs
f_anglodesi.faith: Secular and Sikh families; many secular
f_anglodesi.desc: The London Anglo-Desi are a fusion people of 2240 from Home Counties Commonwealth: English and Punjabi Londoners on the higher boroughs, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes English and Punjabi. In faith they are Sikh by family, and many are secular. They number about 4.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Home Counties Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

garo_khasi.name: Garo and Khasi
garo_khasi.desc: In the Meghalaya hills live the Garo and Khasi, a people of about 4.3 million in 2240. They speak Garo, Khasi, and most are Christian or Niam Khasi. They are strongest in West Bengal. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

sami.name: Sami
sami.desc: The Sami are the people of Sápmi, and in 2240 they number about 4.2 million. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. Their language is Sami. In faith most are Lutheran or Sami tradition. Their strongholds are Lapland-Finnmark, Norrbotten, Kola. The warming made their northern lands milder and busier than ever, and ice-free seas opened new ports.

tsonga.name: Tsonga
tsonga.desc: In Limpopo live the Tsonga, a people of about 4.2 million in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Xitsonga. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Highveld Commonwealth, Limpopo, Manica-Gaza. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_somalinordic.name: Twin Cities Somali-Nordics
f_somalinordic.faith: Sunni Muslim and Lutheran heritage families; many secular
f_somalinordic.desc: The people of Superior Sector are the Twin Cities Somali-Nordics, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Somalis and Scandinavians families met and married. At home they speak Somali and Swedish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Lutheran heritage by family, and many are secular. About 4.2 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Superior Sector. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

mizo_chin.name: Mizo and Chin
mizo_chin.desc: The people of the Lushai and Chin hills are the Mizo and Chin, about 4.2 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. They speak Mizo, Chin languages, and most are Christian. They are strongest in Ganga Delta Commonwealth, Sagaing. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_afroasian.name: Atlanta Afro-Asians
f_afroasian.note: African American and Korean southern metropolis
f_afroasian.language: American English and Korean (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_afroasian.faith: Protestant (Black churches) and Secular families; many secular
f_afroasian.desc: The Atlanta Afro-Asians are a fusion people of 2240 from Muskogee Sector: African American and Korean southern metropolis, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes American English and Korean. In faith they are Protestant (Black churches) by family, and many are secular. About 4.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Muskogee Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_ukrbrazil.name: Paraná Slavo-Brazilians
f_ukrbrazil.language: Ukrainian and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_ukrbrazil.faith: Orthodox and Greek Catholic and Catholic families; many secular
f_ukrbrazil.strong: Sao Paulo Captaincy, Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy
f_ukrbrazil.desc: The people of Sao Paulo Captaincy are the Paraná Slavo-Brazilians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Ukrainians and Brazilians families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Ukrainian and Brazilian Portuguese. In faith they are Orthodox or Greek Catholic or Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 4.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Sao Paulo Captaincy, Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_polonia.name: Great Lakes Polonia
f_polonia.note: Polish and Anglo lake-shore industrial towns
f_polonia.language: Polish and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_polonia.faith: Roman Catholic and Protestant families; many secular
f_polonia.desc: The people of Illinoia Sector are the Great Lakes Polonia, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Poles and Anglo-Americans families met and married. At home they speak Polish and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Protestant by family, and many are secular. About 4.0 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Illinoia Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

galician.name: Galicians
galician.desc: The people of Galicia are the Galicians, about 4.0 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Galician. In faith most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Castilian Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

gilaki.name: Gilaks and Mazandaranis
gilaki.desc: The people of Caspian shore of Iran are the Gilaks and Mazandaranis, about 3.9 million strong in 2240. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. Their language is Gilaki. In faith most are Shia Muslim. Their strongholds are Alborz Commonwealth, East Azerbaijan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

f_fulbehausa.name: Sahel Solar Fulbe-Hausa
f_fulbehausa.desc: The people of Bauchi State are the Sahel Solar Fulbe-Hausa, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Fula and Hausa families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Fula. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 3.9 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Bauchi State, Zinder, Zamfara State. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

ncaucasian.name: Other North Caucasians
ncaucasian.note: Chechnya, Dagestan and the northern slope
ncaucasian.language: Adyghe, Lezgian and other Caucasian tongues
ncaucasian.desc: In Chechnya, Dagestan and the northern slope live the Other North Caucasians, a people of about 3.8 million in 2240. They are an ancient mountain people of the Caucasus, whose many languages are found nowhere else on Earth. Their language is Adyghe. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Kura Commonwealth, Daghestan, Kuban Commonwealth. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

buryat.name: Buryats
buryat.desc: The Buryats are the people of Lake Baikal, and in 2240 they number about 3.8 million. Their ancestors once rode with the largest land empire in history, and the steppe still shapes their way of life. Their language is Buryat. In faith most are Tibetan Buddhist or shamanist. They are strongest in Barguzin, Baikalia, Nerchinsk. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

f_taif.name: Hejaz Spaceport Clans
f_taif.note: Hejazi and Egyptian highland launch-town families
f_taif.language: Najdi and Hejazi Arabic and Egyptian Arabic (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_taif.desc: The people of Makkah Emirate are the Hejaz Spaceport Clans, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Najdi and Hejazi Arabs and Egyptians families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Najdi and Hejazi Arabic and Egyptian Arabic. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 3.8 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Makkah Emirate. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

timorese.name: Timorese, Florenese and Moluccans
timorese.strong: East Nusa Tenggara, East Java, Ambon Commonwealth
timorese.desc: In Lesser Sundas, Timor, Moluccas live the Timorese, Florenese and Moluccans, a people of about 3.7 million in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Tetum. In faith most are Catholic or Protestant. Their strongholds are East Nusa Tenggara, East Java, Ambon Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

jewish.name: Israelis
jewish.desc: The Israelis are the people of Israel, and in 2240 they number about 3.7 million. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Hebrew is their language, and most of them are Judaism or secular. They are strongest in Damascus Capital District, Ma'an. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

albanian.name: Albanians
albanian.desc: The people of Albania, Kosovo are the Albanians, about 3.6 million strong in 2240. Their language forms a branch of the Indo-European family all of its own, older than the borders drawn around it. Albanian is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim, Orthodox or Catholic. They are strongest in Attic Commonwealth, Pomoravski-Berat. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_porteno.name: Porteño Exiles
f_porteno.note: Rioplatense and Italian families resettled in Córdoba from drowned Buenos Aires
f_porteno.language: Rioplatense Spanish and Italian (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_porteno.desc: In Cordoba, Rioplatenses and Italians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Porteño Exiles. At home they speak Rioplatense Spanish and Italian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 3.5 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Cordoba, La Rioja. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_planalto.name: Planalto Orbital Families
f_planalto.language: Brazilian Portuguese and Korean (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_planalto.faith: Catholic and Secular families; many secular
f_planalto.desc: The people of Planalto Federal District are the Planalto Orbital Families, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Brazilians and Koreans families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Brazilian Portuguese and Korean. In faith they are Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 3.5 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Planalto Federal District. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

lozi_tonga.name: Lozi and Tonga
lozi_tonga.desc: The people of Upper Zambezi, Southern Province are the Lozi and Tonga, about 3.5 million strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Silozi, Chitonga, and most are Christian. They are strongest in Northwestern-Western, Zambezi Commonwealth, Cuando Cubango. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

amhara.name: Amhara
amhara.desc: The people of the Ethiopian and Eritrean highlands are the Amhara, about 3.5 million strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Amharic, and most are Ethiopian Orthodox. They are strongest in Tigray-Gash-Barka, Shewa Commonwealth, Amhara. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

ticuna_shipibo.name: Ticuna and Shipibo
ticuna_shipibo.strong: Lima Commonwealth, Loreto March, Amazonas Captaincy
ticuna_shipibo.desc: The people of Upper Amazon are the Ticuna and Shipibo, about 3.5 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Ticuna is their language, and most of them are Traditional or Christian. Their strongholds are Lima Commonwealth, Loreto March, Amazonas Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

hazara.name: Hazaras
hazara.desc: The Hazaras are the people of Hazarajat, and in 2240 they number about 3.4 million. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. Their language is Hazaragi. In faith most are Shia Muslim. They are strongest in Indus Capital Territory, Ghor-Urozgan March. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

herero_nama.name: Herero, Nama and San
herero_nama.desc: The Herero, Nama and San are the people of Namib and Kalahari, and in 2240 they number about 3.4 million. Among them are the descendants of the Khoe and San, the oldest peoples of southern Africa, and of the Herero cattle nations. Their language is Otjiherero. In faith most are Christian or ancestral. They are strongest in Karas-Hardap, Ghanzi-Kgalagadi, Northern Cape. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

sahrawi.name: Sahrawis
sahrawi.strong: Oued Ed-Dahab Wilaya, Tindouf Wilaya, Santa Cruz de Tenerife
sahrawi.desc: In Western Sahara live the Sahrawis, a people of about 3.4 million in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Hassaniya Arabic is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Oued Ed-Dahab Wilaya, Tindouf Wilaya, Santa Cruz de Tenerife. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_andalusi.name: Neo-Andalusis
f_andalusi.language: Spanish and Maghrebi Arabic (Darija) (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_andalusi.faith: Roman Catholic and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_andalusi.desc: The Neo-Andalusis are a fusion people of 2240 from Caceres-Badajoz: Spanish and Maghrebi Andalusian towns, grown into one community. At home they speak Spanish and Maghrebi Arabic, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 3.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Caceres-Badajoz. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_euroanatolian.name: Bosporus Euro-Anatolians
f_euroanatolian.note: Turkish and Greek Istanbul hill quarters
f_euroanatolian.faith: Sunni Muslim and Greek Orthodox families; many secular
f_euroanatolian.desc: In Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet, Turks and Greeks families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Bosporus Euro-Anatolians. Their everyday speech mixes Turkish and Greek. In faith they are Sunni Muslim or Greek Orthodox by family, and many are secular. They number about 3.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Manisa-Balikesir Vilayet. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_caspian.name: Tehran Caspian Synthesis
f_caspian.desc: The people of Alborz Commonwealth are the Tehran Caspian Synthesis, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Persians and Azerbaijanis families met and married. At home they speak Persian and Azerbaijani, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Shia Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 3.2 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Alborz Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

nepali.name: Nepalis
nepali.strong: Uttar Pradesh, Karnali Zone, Lhasa Commonwealth
nepali.desc: The Nepalis are the people of Himalayan foothills, and in 2240 they number about 3.2 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Nepali. In faith most are Hindu or Buddhist. Their strongholds are Uttar Pradesh, Karnali Zone, Lhasa Commonwealth. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

sicilian.name: Sicilians
sicilian.desc: The Sicilians are the people of Sicily, Calabria, and in 2240 they number about 3.1 million. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. They speak Sicilian, Italian, and most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Potenza-Foggia. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_uyghan.name: Silk Corridor Uyghan
f_uyghan.faith: Sunni Muslim and Secular families; many secular
f_uyghan.desc: The people of Tianshan Commonwealth are the Silk Corridor Uyghan, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Uyghurs and Northern Han families met and married. At home they speak Uyghur and Mandarin, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 3.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Tianshan Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_indoarab.name: Gulf Indo-Arabs
f_indoarab.note: Najdi Arab and Malayali Riyadh families
f_indoarab.language: Najdi and Hejazi Arabic and Malayalam (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_indoarab.faith: Sunni Muslim and Hindu families; many secular
f_indoarab.desc: The people of Najd Commonwealth are the Gulf Indo-Arabs, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Najdi and Hejazi Arabs and Malayalis families met and married. At home they speak Najdi and Hejazi Arabic and Malayalam, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 3.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Najd Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

hui.name: Hui
hui.strong: Gansu Circuit, Shaanxi Circuit, Ningxia Circuit
hui.desc: The people of Ningxia, Gansu are the Hui, about 3.1 million strong in 2240. They belong to the Han Chinese, whose written language and civilisation run unbroken for more than three thousand years. They speak Mandarin, and most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Gansu Circuit, Shaanxi Circuit, Ningxia Circuit. Shanghai, Tianjin and the old coastal plain went under the rising sea, and their people moved inland, to the hills and the new northern cities.

purepecha.name: Purépecha
purepecha.desc: In the Michoacán plateau live the Purépecha, a people of about 3.1 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Purépecha, and most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Zacatecas-Jalisco. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

ugric.name: Khanty, Mansi and Nenets
ugric.note: Ob and Yamal; a minority since the gas and grain booms
ugric.desc: The Khanty, Mansi and Nenets are the people of Ob and Yamal, and in 2240 they number about 3.0 million. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. They speak Khanty, Mansi, Nenets, and most are Animist or Orthodox. Their strongholds are Yamal, Ugra, Iset Commonwealth. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

bosniak.name: Bosniaks
bosniak.strong: Potenza-Foggia, Belgrade Federal District, Banja Luka
bosniak.desc: The people of Central Bosnia, Sandžak are the Bosniaks, about 2.9 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Bosnian is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Potenza-Foggia, Belgrade Federal District, Banja Luka. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_paris_viet.name: Seine Viet-Gauls
f_paris_viet.faith: Secular and Folk religion families; many secular
f_paris_viet.desc: The Seine Viet-Gauls are a fusion people of 2240 from Ile-de-France Commonwealth: French and Vietnamese Île-de-France families, grown into one community. At home they speak French and Vietnamese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Folk religion by family, and many are secular. About 2.9 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Ile-de-France Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

polynesian.name: Pacific Islanders
polynesian.desc: The Pacific Islanders are the people of Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and in 2240 they number about 2.9 million. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Samoan. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Owhyhee Sector, North-South, Central-Northern. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_levcarioca.name: Serra Levantine Cariocas
f_levcarioca.note: Levantine and Brazilian merchants moved up to the Petrópolis serra from drowned Rio
f_levcarioca.language: Levantine Arabic and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_levcarioca.faith: Sunni Muslim and Catholic families; many secular
f_levcarioca.desc: In Minas Gerais Captaincy, Levantine Arabs and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Serra Levantine Cariocas. At home they speak Levantine Arabic and Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.9 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Minas Gerais Captaincy. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

mbundu.name: Mbundu
mbundu.desc: The Mbundu are the people of Luanda hinterland, and in 2240 they number about 2.8 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Kimbundu, Portuguese, and most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Malanje-Bie. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

batak.name: Batak
batak.desc: The Batak are the people of the Lake Toba highlands, and in 2240 they number about 2.8 million. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Batak is their language, and most of them are Protestant or Muslim. Their strongholds are Deli Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

aymara.name: Aymara
aymara.strong: Beni March, Potosi March, Cusco Departament March
aymara.desc: The people of Altiplano are the Aymara, about 2.8 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Aymara. In faith most are Catholic with Andean tradition. They are strongest in Beni March, Potosi March, Cusco Departament March. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

lur.name: Lurs and Bakhtiari
lur.desc: The Lurs and Bakhtiari are the people of Zagros, and in 2240 they number about 2.8 million. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. Luri is their language, and most of them are Shia Muslim. They are strongest in Lorestan-Khuzestan Satrapy. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

ainu.name: Ainu
ainu.desc: The Ainu are the people of Eastern Hokkaido, Kurils, and in 2240 they number about 2.7 million. They are the indigenous people of Japan's north, who held Hokkaido long before the Japanese state reached it. They speak Ainu, Japanese, and most are Ainu faith (kamuy). Their strongholds are Hokkaido Prefecture. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

delta_diaspora.name: Delta diaspora
delta_diaspora.note: Bengali, Burmese and Vietnamese delta refugees in the hill cities they built
delta_diaspora.desc: In Luang Prabang live the Delta diaspora, a people of about 2.7 million in 2240. They speak Bengali, Burmese, Vietnamese, and most are Muslim, Buddhist or Hindu. They are strongest in Luang Prabang, Shan State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_chicago_mx.name: Prairie Mexicanos
f_chicago_mx.note: Mexican and Anglo families of the Midwest's farm cities
f_chicago_mx.language: Mexican Spanish and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_chicago_mx.faith: Roman Catholic and Protestant families; many secular
f_chicago_mx.desc: In Illinoia Sector, Mexicans and Anglo-Americans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Prairie Mexicanos. At home they speak Mexican Spanish and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Protestant by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.7 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Illinoia Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

visayan.name: Visayans
