visayan.desc: In Visayas, Mindanao live the Visayans, a people of about 2.7 million in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Cebuano. In faith most are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Visayana, Mindanaia, Sulu. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

meitei.name: Meitei
meitei.desc: In the Manipur valley live the Meitei, a people of about 2.7 million in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Meitei. In faith most are Hindu or Sanamahism. They are strongest in Ganga Delta Commonwealth, Kachin State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

ashaninka.name: Asháninka
ashaninka.desc: The Asháninka are the people of Peruvian selva, and in 2240 they number about 2.7 million. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Asháninka is their language, and most of them are Traditional or Christian. They are strongest in Lima Commonwealth. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

afro_brazilian.name: Afro-Brazilians
afro_brazilian.desc: The people of Bahia and the Recôncavo are the Afro-Brazilians, about 2.7 million strong in 2240. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Their language is Brazilian Portuguese. In faith most are Candomblé, Catholic or Evangelical. They are strongest in Bahia Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_obuzbek.name: Ob Neo-Uzbeks
f_obuzbek.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_obuzbek.desc: The Ob Neo-Uzbeks are a fusion people of 2240 from Ob Commonwealth: Uzbek and Russian Novosibirsk-belt workers, grown into one community. At home they speak Uzbek and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.6 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Ob Commonwealth, Kuznetsk, Oirotia II. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

ladakhi.name: Ladakhis and Baltis
ladakhi.strong: Himachal Pradesh, Gorno-Badakhshan, Jammu and Kashmir
ladakhi.desc: In Ladakh, Baltistan live the Ladakhis and Baltis, a people of about 2.6 million in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Ladakhi is their language, and most of them are Tibetan Buddhist or Shia Muslim. They are strongest in Himachal Pradesh, Gorno-Badakhshan, Jammu and Kashmir. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

maithili.name: Maithils
maithili.desc: The Maithils are the people of Mithila, and in 2240 they number about 2.6 million. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Maithili. In faith most are Hindu. Their strongholds are Jharkhand, Karnali Zone. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_hydrofolk.name: Sichuan Hydrofolk
f_hydrofolk.language: Southwestern Mandarin and Tibetan (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_hydrofolk.faith: Secular and Tibetan Buddhist families; many secular
f_hydrofolk.desc: The people of Chengdu Commonwealth are the Sichuan Hydrofolk, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Southwestern Han and Tibetans families met and married. At home they speak Southwestern Mandarin and Tibetan, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Tibetan Buddhist by family, and many are secular. About 2.5 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Chengdu Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

odia.name: Odias
odia.desc: In Odisha live the Odias, a people of about 2.5 million in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Odia is their language, and most of them are Hindu. Their strongholds are Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

apache_oodham.name: Apache and O'odham
apache_oodham.desc: In the Arizona and New Mexico highlands live the Apache and O'odham, a people of about 2.5 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Apache is their language, and most of them are Native tradition or Christian. They are strongest in Deseret Sector, Sonora. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

lithuanian.name: Lithuanians
lithuanian.desc: In Lithuania live the Lithuanians, a people of about 2.5 million in 2240. Their Baltic language is one of the oldest living branches of the Indo-European family, kept alive through centuries of rule by stronger neighbours. They speak Lithuanian, and most are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Riga Hanse District, Minsk-Gomel, Sambia. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

sardinian.name: Sardinians
sardinian.desc: In Sardinia live the Sardinians, a people of about 2.4 million in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Sardinian. In faith most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in Latium Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_norilsk.name: Norilsk Dome Clans
f_norilsk.note: Russian and Evenk sealed-dome city families
f_norilsk.faith: Orthodox Christian and Shamanist families; many secular
f_norilsk.desc: The Norilsk Dome Clans are a fusion people of 2240 from Yeniseia: Russian and Evenk sealed-dome city families, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Russian and Evenki. In faith they are Orthodox Christian or Shamanist by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.4 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Yeniseia. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

chukchi.name: Chukchi and Koryaks
chukchi.desc: In Chukotka live the Chukchi and Koryaks, a people of about 2.4 million in 2240. They are reindeer herders and sea hunters of the far north-east, the last people of Asia before America. Their language is Chukchi. In faith most are Shamanist. They are strongest in Kamchadalia, Chukchi Land, Kolyma. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

macedonian.name: Macedonians
macedonian.desc: In the Vardar valley live the Macedonians, a people of about 2.4 million in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Macedonian is their language, and most of them are Orthodox Christian. They are strongest in Attic Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_kinshasa.name: Kinshasa Cosmopolitans
f_kinshasa.parents: Kongo and Lingala peoples + Luba and Kasai peoples
f_kinshasa.desc: The people of Pool Commonwealth are the Kinshasa Cosmopolitans, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Kongo and Lingala peoples and Luba and Kasai peoples families met and married. At home they speak Kikongo and Tshiluba, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.4 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Pool Commonwealth, Kongo Central. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_johannesburg_mz.name: Rand Mozambican-Zulus
f_johannesburg_mz.desc: In Highveld Commonwealth, Zulu and Nguni and Tsonga families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Rand Mozambican-Zulus. Their everyday speech mixes isiZulu and Xitsonga. In faith they are Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Highveld Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

kiche.name: K'iche' and Highland Maya
kiche.desc: In the Guatemalan highlands live the K'iche' and Highland Maya, a people of about 2.3 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. K'iche' is their language, and most of them are Catholic or Maya tradition. Their strongholds are Peten Canton. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

ovambo.name: Ovambo and Namibians
ovambo.desc: The Ovambo and Namibians are the people of Northern and central Namibia, and in 2240 they number about 2.3 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Oshiwambo. In faith most are Lutheran Christian. Their strongholds are Karas-Hardap, Huila-Namibe, Cunene. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

songhai.name: Songhai and Zarma
songhai.desc: The people of Niger bend are the Songhai and Zarma, about 2.3 million strong in 2240. They are heirs of the Songhai Empire, which once ruled the Niger bend from Gao and Timbuktu. Songhai is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Mopti, Tahoua-Tillaberi, Zamfara State. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

beja.name: Beja
beja.strong: Al Qadarif Nome, Tigray-Gash-Barka, Red Sea Nome
beja.desc: The Beja are the people of the Red Sea hills, and in 2240 they number about 2.3 million. They are a Cushitic people of the Horn of Africa, herders and traders on one of the oldest routes between Africa and Arabia. Beja (Bedawi) is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Al Qadarif Nome, Tigray-Gash-Barka, Red Sea Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

kashmiri.name: Kashmiris
kashmiri.strong: Himachal Pradesh, Indus Capital Territory, Jammu and Kashmir
kashmiri.desc: The people of Vale of Kashmir are the Kashmiris, about 2.3 million strong in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Their language is Kashmiri. In faith most are Muslim or Hindu (Pandits). They are strongest in Himachal Pradesh, Indus Capital Territory, Jammu and Kashmir. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

papuan.name: Papuans
papuan.strong: Coral Sea Commonwealth, Humboldt Bay Commonwealth, West Papua
papuan.desc: The Papuans are the people of New Guinea, and in 2240 they number about 2.2 million. Their ancestors reached New Guinea more than forty thousand years ago and became some of the world's first farmers. Papuan languages is their language, and most of them are Christian or ancestral faiths. Their strongholds are Coral Sea Commonwealth, Humboldt Bay Commonwealth, West Papua. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

makua.name: Makua and Mozambicans
makua.desc: The Makua and Mozambicans are the people of Northern and central Mozambique, and in 2240 they number about 2.2 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Makhuwa. In faith most are Muslim or Christian. They are strongest in Tete, Zambezia, Manica-Gaza. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_manila_cn.name: Luzon Tsinoys
f_manila_cn.note: Filipino and Min Chinese merchant families
f_manila_cn.parents: Tagalog and Luzon peoples + Min Chinese
f_manila_cn.faith: Roman Catholic and Folk religion (Mazu) families; many secular
f_manila_cn.desc: In Maynila Commonwealth, Tagalog and Luzon peoples and Min Chinese families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Luzon Tsinoys. At home they speak Tagalog and Hokkien, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Folk religion (Mazu) by family, and many are secular. About 2.2 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Maynila Commonwealth, Luzonia, Ibalon. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_panafrican.name: Ibadan Pan-Africans
f_panafrican.note: Yoruba and Igbo megacity people moved inland from drowned Lagos
f_panafrican.desc: In Abuja Federal Territory, Yoruba and Igbo families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Ibadan Pan-Africans. At home they speak Yoruba and Igbo, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Christian by family, and many are secular. About 2.2 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Abuja Federal Territory. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

pamiri.name: Pamiris
pamiri.language: Shughni, Wakhi and other Pamiri tongues
pamiri.desc: In Badakhshan live the Pamiris, a people of about 2.2 million in 2240. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. They speak Shughni, Wakhi and other Pamiri tongues, and most are Ismaili Muslim. Their strongholds are Gorno-Badakhshan, Indus Capital Territory. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

f_zhuangviet.name: Guangxi Zhuang-Viet
f_zhuangviet.faith: Mo folk religion and Folk religion families; many secular
f_zhuangviet.desc: The people of Guangxi Circuit are the Guangxi Zhuang-Viet, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Zhuang and Vietnamese families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Zhuang and Vietnamese. In faith they are Mo folk religion or Folk religion by family, and many are secular. About 2.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Guangxi Circuit. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

bai_naxi.name: Bai and Naxi
bai_naxi.desc: The people of Dali, Lijiang are the Bai and Naxi, about 2.1 million strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Bai. In faith most are Dongba or Buddhist. They are strongest in Yunnan Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_xiangmiao.name: Hunan Xiang-Miao
f_xiangmiao.language: Xiang Chinese and Hmong-Mien languages (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_xiangmiao.faith: Folk religion and Animist families; many secular
f_xiangmiao.desc: The Hunan Xiang-Miao are a fusion people of 2240 from Hunan Circuit: Xiang and Miao terrace-farming towns, grown into one community. At home they speak Xiang Chinese and Hmong-Mien languages, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Folk religion or Animist by family, and many are secular. About 2.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Hunan Circuit, Guizhou Circuit. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

shuar_kichwa.name: Shuar and Amazonian Kichwa
shuar_kichwa.desc: In Ecuadorian Oriente live the Shuar and Amazonian Kichwa, a people of about 2.1 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Shuar. In faith most are Traditional or Catholic. They are strongest in Amazonas-Caqueta Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_karachi.name: Sindh Ridge Muhajirs
f_karachi.note: Sindhi and Hindustani families moved up from drowned Karachi
f_karachi.faith: Muslim and Hindu families; many secular
f_karachi.desc: The people of Sindh March are the Sindh Ridge Muhajirs, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Sindhis and Hindustanis families met and married. At home they speak Sindhi and Hindi-Urdu, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Muslim or Hindu by family, and many are secular. They number about 2.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Sindh March. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

baoule.name: Baoulé
baoule.desc: The people of the Central Ivory Coast are the Baoulé, about 2.0 million strong in 2240. They are a Kwa people of the West African forest, heirs of kingdoms built on gold, kola and trade. Baoulé is their language, and most of them are Christian or Baoulé faith. They are strongest in Savanes-Zanzan. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

moldovan.name: Moldovans
moldovan.desc: The people of Bessarabia are the Moldovans, about 2.0 million strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is Romanian (Moldovan). In faith most are Orthodox Christian. Their strongholds are Suceava-Bacau, Wallachian Commonwealth, Kirovohrad-Vinnytsia. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_taihan.name: Yunnan Tai-Han
f_taihan.note: Dai and Han highland tea-and-solar towns
f_taihan.language: Tai Lü and Southwestern Mandarin (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_taihan.faith: Theravada Buddhist and Secular families; many secular
f_taihan.desc: In Yunnan Circuit, Dai and Southwestern Han families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Yunnan Tai-Han. Their everyday speech mixes Tai Lü and Southwestern Mandarin. In faith they are Theravada Buddhist by family, and many are secular. About 1.9 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Yunnan Circuit. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

turkana.name: Turkana and Karamojong
turkana.desc: The people of Lake Turkana, Karamoja are the Turkana and Karamojong, about 1.9 million strong in 2240. They are a Nilotic people, cattle herders of the Nile and the Rift, tall, proud and stubborn about their land. Turkana is their language, and most of them are Traditional or Christian. They are strongest in Rift Valley Commonwealth, Eastern Equatoria. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_nairobi.name: Nairobi Silicon Swahili
f_nairobi.note: Kikuyu and Indian highland tech city
f_nairobi.faith: Christian and Hindu families; many secular
f_nairobi.desc: The people of Rift Valley Commonwealth are the Nairobi Silicon Swahili, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Kikuyu and Kenyan highlanders and Hindustanis families met and married. At home they speak Kikuyu and Hindi-Urdu, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Christian or Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 1.8 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Rift Valley Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

wichi_qom.name: Wichí and Qom
wichi_qom.strong: Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Santiago del Estero, Salta March
wichi_qom.desc: In Gran Chaco live the Wichí and Qom, a people of about 1.8 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Wichí. In faith most are Anglican or traditional. Their strongholds are Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Santiago del Estero, Salta March. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

senufo.name: Senufo
senufo.desc: The people of the Northern Ivory Coast are the Senufo, about 1.8 million strong in 2240. They are a Gur-speaking people of the West African savannah, farmers whose chiefdoms resisted the great empires around them. They speak Senufo, and most are Senufo faith or Muslim. Their strongholds are Savanes-Zanzan. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

lunda_chokwe.name: Lunda and Chokwe
lunda_chokwe.desc: The Lunda and Chokwe are the people of the Lunda plateau, and in 2240 they number about 1.8 million. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Lunda. In faith most are Christian. They are strongest in Pool Commonwealth, Katanga, Moxico. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_somalinorse.name: Oslo Somali-Norse
f_somalinorse.faith: Lutheran heritage and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_somalinorse.desc: The Oslo Somali-Norse are a fusion people of 2240 from Dalarna: Somali and Norwegian Oslo families, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Swedish and Somali. In faith they are Lutheran heritage or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 1.8 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Dalarna, Oppland. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

tay_nung.name: Tày and Nùng
tay_nung.desc: The people of the Northern Vietnam highlands are the Tày and Nùng, about 1.8 million strong in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. Tày is their language, and most of them are Folk religion. They are strongest in Luang Prabang. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

f_santiago.name: Santiago Andean-Mapuche
f_santiago.language: Chilean Spanish and Mapudungun (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_santiago.faith: Roman Catholic and Mapuche faith families; many secular
f_santiago.desc: In La Pampa, Chileans and Mapuche families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Santiago Andean-Mapuche. At home they speak Chilean Spanish and Mapudungun, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Mapuche faith by family, and many are secular. About 1.8 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in La Pampa. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

basque.name: Basques
basque.desc: In Basque Country, Navarre live the Basques, a people of about 1.7 million in 2240. Their language is older than any other in western Europe and related to none of them, a survivor from before the Indo-Europeans came. Their language is Basque. In faith most are Catholic or secular. They are strongest in Zaragoza-Teruel. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

slovak.name: Slovaks
slovak.desc: The people of Slovakia are the Slovaks, about 1.7 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were among the Slavic peoples who spread across eastern and central Europe in the early Middle Ages and later built kingdoms, empires and, in the twentieth century, nations of their own. Slovak is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic. Their strongholds are Banska Bystrica March, Alba-Bihor. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_teuto.name: Teuto-Catarinenses
f_teuto.note: German and Brazilian southern valley towns
f_teuto.language: German and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_teuto.faith: Protestant and Catholic families; many secular
f_teuto.desc: The Teuto-Catarinenses are a fusion people of 2240 from Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy: German and Brazilian southern valley towns, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes German and Brazilian Portuguese. In faith they are Protestant or Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 1.7 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Rio Grande do Sul Captaincy. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

gurage_sidama.name: Gurage, Sidama and Wolaita
gurage_sidama.desc: The Gurage, Sidama and Wolaita are the people of the Southern Ethiopian highlands, and in 2240 they number about 1.7 million. They are the peoples of the southern Ethiopian highlands, farmers of ensete and coffee on some of Africa's richest soil. They speak Gurage, Sidama, Wolaytta, and most are Orthodox, Protestant or Muslim. Their strongholds are Shewa Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

dagomba.name: Dagomba and Mole peoples
dagomba.desc: The people of Northern Ghana are the Dagomba and Mole peoples, about 1.7 million strong in 2240. They are a Gur-speaking people of the West African savannah, farmers whose chiefdoms resisted the great empires around them. They speak Dagbani, and most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Northern-Brong-Ahafo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

alaskan.name: Alaskans
alaskan.desc: The people of the Alaska interior are the Alaskans, about 1.7 million strong in 2240. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. American English is their language, and most of them are Christian or secular. They are strongest in Alyeska Proper, Klondike. The thaw opened the north of their land to farming, and new towns grew where there had been permafrost.

f_borderfolk.name: Bug River Borderfolk
f_borderfolk.faith: Roman Catholic and Orthodox and Greek Catholic families; many secular
f_borderfolk.desc: The people of Vistula Commonwealth are the Bug River Borderfolk, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Poles and Ukrainians families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Polish and Ukrainian. In faith they are Roman Catholic or Orthodox or Greek Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 1.7 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Vistula Commonwealth, Brest-Lviv. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

banyarwanda.name: Banyarwanda and Barundi
banyarwanda.desc: The people of Rwanda, Burundi are the Banyarwanda and Barundi, about 1.7 million strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Kinyarwanda is their language, and most of them are Christian. They are strongest in North Kivu, Maniema. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

dan.name: Dan and Kru peoples
dan.desc: The people of Ivory Coast and Liberian forest are the Dan and Kru peoples, about 1.6 million strong in 2240. They are the forest peoples of the Liberian and Ivorian hills, keepers of masks and secret societies. Their language is Dan. In faith most are Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Northern, Savanes-Zanzan. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

kpelle.name: Kpelle and Liberian peoples
kpelle.desc: In Liberia live the Kpelle and Liberian peoples, a people of about 1.6 million in 2240. They descend from the Mande of the old Mali Empire, whose griots still keep its history in song. Kpelle is their language, and most of them are Christian or Poro tradition. They are strongest in Northern. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_pantanal.name: Pantanal Guaraní-Brazilians
f_pantanal.language: Guarani and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_pantanal.faith: Guarani faith and Catholic families; many secular
f_pantanal.strong: Mato Grosso do Sul Captaincy, Santa Cruz March, Mato Grosso Captaincy
f_pantanal.desc: In Mato Grosso do Sul Captaincy, Guaraní peoples and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Pantanal Guaraní-Brazilians. At home they speak Guarani and Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Guarani faith or Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 1.6 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Mato Grosso do Sul Captaincy, Santa Cruz March, Mato Grosso Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_phoenix.name: Desert Dome Arizonans
f_phoenix.note: Anglo and Mexican families of the solar-domed desert cities
f_phoenix.language: American English and Mexican Spanish (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_phoenix.faith: Protestant and Roman Catholic families; many secular
f_phoenix.desc: The Desert Dome Arizonans are a fusion people of 2240 from Deseret Sector: Anglo and Mexican families of the solar-domed desert cities, grown into one community. At home they speak American English and Mexican Spanish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Protestant or Roman Catholic by family, and many are secular. About 1.6 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Deseret Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

dai.name: Dai
dai.desc: In Xishuangbanna, Dehong live the Dai, a people of about 1.6 million in 2240. They are a Tai-speaking people, rice farmers of the valleys who spread south from southern China a thousand years ago. Tai Lü is their language, and most of them are Theravada Buddhist. They are strongest in Shan State, Yunnan Circuit. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

lakota.name: Lakota and Plains nations
lakota.desc: The people of Dakotas are the Lakota and Plains nations, about 1.5 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Lakota. In faith most are Lakota tradition or Christian. They are strongest in Absaroka Sector. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

f_santacruz.name: Camba Mennonite-Bolivians
f_santacruz.language: Andean Spanish and Plautdietsch (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_santacruz.faith: Roman Catholic and Mennonite families; many secular
f_santacruz.desc: The people of Santa Cruz March are the Camba Mennonite-Bolivians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Andean Mestizos and Chaco Mennonites families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Andean Spanish and Plautdietsch. In faith they are Roman Catholic or Mennonite by family, and many are secular. They number about 1.5 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Santa Cruz March. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

druze.name: Druze
druze.desc: In Jabal al-Druze, Mount Lebanon, Carmel live the Druze, a people of about 1.5 million in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Levantine Arabic, and most are Druze faith. They are strongest in Damascus Capital District, Al Anbar. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_tusan.name: Tusán
f_tusan.language: Andean Spanish and Cantonese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_tusan.faith: Roman Catholic and Folk religion families; many secular
f_tusan.desc: In Lima Commonwealth, Andean Mestizos and Cantonese families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Tusán. At home they speak Andean Spanish and Cantonese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Folk religion by family, and many are secular. About 1.5 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Lima Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

assyrian.name: Assyrians
assyrian.desc: The people of Nineveh plain, Hakkari are the Assyrians, about 1.5 million strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Their language is Neo-Aramaic. In faith most are Assyrian and Chaldean Christian. They are strongest in Two Rivers Commonwealth. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_yenisei.name: Yenisei Sino-Siberians
f_yenisei.language: Mandarin and Siberian Russian with Chinese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_yenisei.desc: The Yenisei Sino-Siberians are a fusion people of 2240 from Yeniseia: Han and Sibiryak hydropower cities, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Mandarin and Siberian Russian with Chinese. In faith they are mostly secular. About 1.5 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Yeniseia, Khongoray. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

maori.name: Maori
maori.desc: The Maori are the people of Aotearoa North Island, and in 2240 they number about 1.4 million. Their ancestors were the Polynesian navigators who found every island of the Pacific with stars, swells and memory. They speak Maori, English, and most are Christian, Ratana or Maori faith. Their strongholds are Te Whanganui Commonwealth, Northland. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

f_huikaz.name: Gansu Hui-Turkic
f_huikaz.desc: The people of Gansu Circuit are the Gansu Hui-Turkic, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Hui and Kazakhs families met and married. At home they speak Mandarin and Kazakh, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 1.4 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Gansu Circuit, Ningxia Circuit. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

tatar.name: Volga Tatars
tatar.desc: The Volga Tatars are the people of Middle Volga, and in 2240 they number about 1.4 million. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Tatar is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Kazan Commonwealth, Zhiguli-Simbirsk, Vyatka. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_dearborn.name: Great Lakes Arab-Americans
f_dearborn.language: Levantine Arabic and American English (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_dearborn.faith: Sunni Muslim and Protestant families; many secular
f_dearborn.desc: The people of Westsylvania Sector are the Great Lakes Arab-Americans, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Levantine Arabs and Anglo-Americans families met and married. At home they speak Levantine Arabic and American English, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Protestant by family, and many are secular. About 1.4 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Westsylvania Sector. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

wayuu.name: Wayuu
wayuu.desc: The people of Guajira are the Wayuu, about 1.4 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Wayuunaiki, and most are Wayuu faith or Catholic. They are strongest in Barinas Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

roma.name: Roma
roma.note: Scattered across the Balkans and Pannonia
roma.desc: The people of Scattered across the Balkans and Pannonia are the Roma, about 1.3 million strong in 2240. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. Romani is their language, and most of them are Christian or Muslim. Their strongholds are East Macedonia and Thrace. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

f_sakharus.name: Sakha Diamond Mix
f_sakharus.faith: Aar Aiyy (Sakha faith) and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_sakharus.desc: In Olonkho, Sakha and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Sakha Diamond Mix. At home they speak Sakha, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Aar Aiyy (Sakha faith) or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 1.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Olonkho. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_dakar.name: Senegambian Exile Creoles
f_dakar.note: Wolof and French families resettled inland from drowned Dakar
f_dakar.faith: Sufi Muslim and Secular families; many secular
f_dakar.desc: In Siguiri Prefecture, Wolof and Senegambians and French families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Senegambian Exile Creoles. Their everyday speech mixes Wolof and French. In faith they are Sufi Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 1.3 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Siguiri Prefecture. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_sinoaussie.name: Pacific-Asian Australians
f_sinoaussie.language: Australian English and Mandarin (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_sinoaussie.desc: The Pacific-Asian Australians are a fusion people of 2240 from Cumberland: Anglo-Australian and Han Sydney-basin families, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Australian English and Mandarin. In faith they are mostly secular. They number about 1.3 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Cumberland. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_rome.name: Roman Afro-Italians
f_rome.faith: Roman Catholic and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_rome.desc: The Roman Afro-Italians are a fusion people of 2240 from Potenza-Foggia: Italian and Somali Roman families, grown into one community. At home they speak Italian and Somali, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 1.3 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Potenza-Foggia, Latium Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_murmansk.name: Murmansk Arctic Portfolk
f_murmansk.note: Russian and Norwegian ice-free port people
f_murmansk.faith: Orthodox Christian and Lutheran heritage families; many secular
f_murmansk.desc: In Kola, Russians and Scandinavians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Murmansk Arctic Portfolk. At home they speak Russian and Swedish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Orthodox Christian or Lutheran heritage by family, and many are secular. About 1.3 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Kola, Lapland-Finnmark. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

dayak.name: Dayak and Iban
dayak.desc: The Dayak and Iban are the people of the Borneo interior, and in 2240 they number about 1.3 million. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Dayak and Iban languages is their language, and most of them are Kaharingan or Christian. Their strongholds are Sabah, Sarawak River Commonwealth, Paragua. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

breton.name: Bretons
breton.desc: The people of Brittany are the Bretons, about 1.2 million strong in 2240. They are heirs of the Celtic peoples who once held most of western Europe and who held on longest at its Atlantic edge. They speak Breton, French, and most are Catholic or secular. Their strongholds are Home Counties Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

tigrinya.name: Tigrinya
tigrinya.desc: In Eritrean highlands, Tigray live the Tigrinya, a people of about 1.2 million in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. Their language is Tigrinya. In faith most are Orthodox Christian. They are strongest in Tigray-Gash-Barka. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

chuvash.name: Chuvash
chuvash.desc: In Middle Volga live the Chuvash, a people of about 1.2 million in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Their language is Chuvash. In faith most are Orthodox or Vattisen Yaly. They are strongest in Zhiguli-Simbirsk, Meshchera, Kazan Commonwealth. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

chaoui_rif.name: Chaouis and Riffians
chaoui_rif.desc: In Aurès and the Rif live the Chaouis and Riffians, a people of about 1.2 million in 2240. They are the indigenous people of North Africa, older on their land than every empire that came to rule it. Their language is Chaouia. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Ouargla Wilaya, Algiers Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

qeqchi.name: Q'eqchi'
qeqchi.desc: The people of Alta Verapaz are the Q'eqchi', about 1.2 million strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Q'eqchi', and most are Catholic or Maya tradition. They are strongest in Peten Canton. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

sara.name: Sara
sara.desc: The people of Southern Chad are the Sara, about 1.2 million strong in 2240. They are a Nilo-Saharan people of the dry lands between the Nile and Lake Chad. Their language is Sara. In faith most are Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Haute-Kotto Prefecture, Guera. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_cairoorbital.name: Cairo Highland Spacers
f_cairoorbital.note: Egyptian and Levantine engineers of the Muqattam launch towers
f_cairoorbital.language: Egyptian Arabic and Levantine Arabic (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_cairoorbital.desc: In Delta Commonwealth, Egyptians and Levantine Arabs families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Cairo Highland Spacers. At home they speak Egyptian Arabic and Levantine Arabic, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 1.1 million of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Delta Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

guna_embera.name: Guna and Emberá
guna_embera.desc: In Darién live the Guna and Emberá, a people of about 1.1 million in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Guna is their language, and most of them are Guna faith or Christian. They are strongest in Canal Free Zone. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

sukuma.name: Sukuma and Nyamwezi
sukuma.desc: In the Tanzanian plateau live the Sukuma and Nyamwezi, a people of about 1.1 million in 2240. They speak Sukuma, Nyamwezi, and most are Christian or traditional. Their strongholds are Tabora, North Kivu, Manyara-Singida. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_koryorus.name: Primorye Koryo-Rus
f_koryorus.note: Korean and Russian Pacific port people
f_koryorus.faith: Secular and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_koryorus.strong: Jilin Circuit, Lukomorye, North Hamgyong Province
f_koryorus.desc: In Jilin Circuit, Koreans and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Primorye Koryo-Rus. At home they speak Korean and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 1.1 million, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Jilin Circuit, Lukomorye, North Hamgyong Province. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

latvian.name: Latvians
latvian.desc: In Latvia live the Latvians, a people of about 1.1 million in 2240. Their Baltic language is one of the oldest living branches of the Indo-European family, kept alive through centuries of rule by stronger neighbours. They speak Latvian, and most are Lutheran or Dievturība. Their strongholds are Riga Hanse District. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

hawaiian.name: Native Hawaiians
hawaiian.desc: The Native Hawaiians are the people of the Hawaiian islands, and in 2240 they number about 1.1 million. Their strongholds are Owhyhee Sector. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

moro.name: Moro peoples

They are strongest in Sulu, Mindanaia. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

sinhalese.name: Sinhalese
sinhalese.desc: The Sinhalese are the people of Sri Lanka, and in 2240 they number about 993 thousand. f_tashkent.name: Tashkent Russo-Uzbeks

You find them above all in Tashkent Capital District. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

mapuche.name: Mapuche

ni_vanuatu.name: Ni-Vanuatu and Solomon Islanders
