Their strongholds are North-South. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

f_acre.name: Acre Andean-Brazilians
f_acre.language: Quechua and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_acre.faith: Catholic with Andean tradition and Catholic families; many secular
f_acre.strong: Beni March, Amazonas Captaincy, Acre March
f_acre.desc: In Beni March, Quechua and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Acre Andean-Brazilians. Their everyday speech mixes Quechua and Brazilian Portuguese. In faith they are Catholic with Andean tradition or Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 963 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Beni March, Amazonas Captaincy, Acre March. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_vietkhmer.name: Highland Viet-Khmer
f_vietkhmer.note: Vietnamese and Khmer delta refugees on the plateau
f_vietkhmer.faith: Folk religion and Theravada Buddhist families; many secular
f_vietkhmer.desc: The people of Gia Lai are the Highland Viet-Khmer, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Vietnamese and Khmer families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Vietnamese and Khmer. In faith they are Folk religion or Theravada Buddhist by family, and many are secular. About 957 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Gia Lai. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

degar.name: Degar (Montagnards)
degar.desc: The people of the Central Highlands are the Degar (Montagnards), about 957 thousand strong in 2240. They are the highland peoples of Indochina, who kept their longhouses and lands while the lowland kingdoms rose and fell. They speak Jarai, Rhade, Bahnar, and most are Protestant or animist. They are strongest in Gia Lai. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

madurese.name: Madurese
madurese.desc: In the Madura, East Java coast live the Madurese, a people of about 947 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Madurese is their language, and most of them are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are East Java. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_dubai.name: Hajar Gulf-Desi
f_dubai.note: Omani and Malayali families of the Hajar foothill cities
f_dubai.language: Omani Arabic and Malayalam (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_dubai.faith: Ibadi Muslim and Hindu families; many secular
f_dubai.desc: The people of Al Wusta Emirate are the Hajar Gulf-Desi, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Omanis and Malayalis families met and married. At home they speak Omani Arabic and Malayalam, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Ibadi Muslim or Hindu by family, and many are secular. About 944 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Al Wusta Emirate. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

bashkir.name: Bashkirs
bashkir.desc: In Southern Urals live the Bashkirs, a people of about 940 thousand in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Their language is Bashkir. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Bashkiria, Yaik, Arkaim-Tobol. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

karen.name: Karen
karen.desc: The Karen are the people of the Karen hills, and in 2240 they number about 921 thousand. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Karen languages. In faith most are Buddhist or Christian. Their strongholds are Shan State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

komi.name: Komi
komi.desc: The Komi are the people of Pechora and Vychegda, and in 2240 they number about 897 thousand. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. They speak Komi, Russian, and most are Orthodox or Old Believer. Their strongholds are Biarmia, Perm Capital District, Vyatka. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_warsaw.name: Vistula Ukraino-Poles
f_warsaw.faith: Roman Catholic and Orthodox and Greek Catholic families; many secular
f_warsaw.desc: The Vistula Ukraino-Poles are a fusion people of 2240 from Vistula Commonwealth: Polish and Ukrainian Warsaw families, grown into one community. At home they speak Polish and Ukrainian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Roman Catholic or Orthodox or Greek Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 883 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Vistula Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_nilenubian.name: Upper Nile Nubians
f_nilenubian.language: Egyptian Arabic and Sudanese Arabic (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_nilenubian.strong: South Sinai Nome, New Valley Nome
f_nilenubian.desc: In South Sinai Nome, Egyptians and Sudanese Arabs and Nubians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Upper Nile Nubians. Their everyday speech mixes Egyptian Arabic and Sudanese Arabic. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 883 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in South Sinai Nome, New Valley Nome. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_gulfcreole.name: Neo-Creoles of the Gulf
f_gulfcreole.note: African American and French Louisianans on the higher ground
f_gulfcreole.language: American English and French (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_gulfcreole.faith: Protestant (Black churches) and Secular families; many secular
f_gulfcreole.desc: The people of Orleans Sector are the Neo-Creoles of the Gulf, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where African Americans and French families met and married. At home they speak American English and French, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Protestant (Black churches) by family, and many are secular. They number about 882 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Orleans Sector. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_sinobrazil.name: Sino-Pernambucanos
f_sinobrazil.note: Han and Brazilian north-east port-and-factory towns
f_sinobrazil.language: Mandarin and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_sinobrazil.faith: Secular and Catholic families; many secular
f_sinobrazil.desc: In Pernambuco Captaincy, Northern Han and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Sino-Pernambucanos. Their everyday speech mixes Mandarin and Brazilian Portuguese. In faith they are Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 851 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Pernambuco Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

udmurt.name: Udmurts
udmurt.strong: Kazan Commonwealth, Perm Capital District, Vyatka
udmurt.desc: The Udmurts are the people of Kama-Vyatka, and in 2240 they number about 816 thousand. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. They speak Udmurt, and most are Orthodox or Udmurt faith. They are strongest in Kazan Commonwealth, Perm Capital District, Vyatka. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

pedi.name: Pedi (Northern Sotho)
pedi.desc: In Sekhukhuneland live the Pedi (Northern Sotho), a people of about 797 thousand in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Sepedi. In faith most are Christian or ancestral. They are strongest in Limpopo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_medan.name: Deli Highland Mix
f_medan.note: Batak, Javanese and Han families of Medan's highlands
f_medan.faith: Protestant and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_medan.strong: Deli Commonwealth, Klang Commonwealth, Surat Thani
f_medan.desc: The Deli Highland Mix are a fusion people of 2240 from Deli Commonwealth: Batak, Javanese and Han families of Medan's highlands, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Batak and Javanese. In faith they are Protestant or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 791 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Deli Commonwealth, Klang Commonwealth, Surat Thani. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_omsk.name: Irtysh Kazakh-Rus
f_omsk.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_omsk.desc: In Irtysh, Kazakhs and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Irtysh Kazakh-Rus. At home they speak Kazakh and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 767 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Irtysh. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

dinka_nuer.name: Dinka and Nuer
dinka_nuer.strong: Western Bahr el Ghazal Nome, North Kordofan Nome, Jonglei
dinka_nuer.desc: In Upper Nile, Bahr el Ghazal live the Dinka and Nuer, a people of about 750 thousand in 2240. They are a Nilotic people, cattle herders of the Nile and the Rift, tall, proud and stubborn about their land. They speak Dinka, Nuer, and most are Christian or traditional. They are strongest in Western Bahr el Ghazal Nome, North Kordofan Nome, Jonglei. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

cajun.name: Acadians and Cajuns
cajun.desc: The people of Louisiana uplands, New Brunswick are the Acadians and Cajuns, about 739 thousand strong in 2240. Their language grew out of the Latin of the Roman Empire, carried by soldiers, settlers and later by the Church. Their language is English. In faith most are Roman Catholic. They are strongest in New Ireland. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

f_addis.name: Addis Pan-Ethiopians
f_addis.faith: Ethiopian Orthodox and Muslim families; many secular
f_addis.desc: The people of Shewa Commonwealth are the Addis Pan-Ethiopians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Amhara and Oromo families met and married. At home they speak Amharic and Oromo, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Ethiopian Orthodox or Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 734 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Shewa Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

kayapo_xavante.name: Kayapó and Xavante
kayapo_xavante.desc: The people of Xingu and Mato Grosso are the Kayapó and Xavante, about 730 thousand strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Kayapó is their language, and most of them are Traditional. They are strongest in Para Captaincy, Mato Grosso Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_afrobahia.name: Neo-Yoruba Bahians
f_afrobahia.note: Afro-Brazilian and Yoruba of the Recôncavo
f_afrobahia.language: Brazilian Portuguese and Yoruba (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_afrobahia.faith: Candomblé and Christian families; many secular
f_afrobahia.desc: The people of Bahia Captaincy are the Neo-Yoruba Bahians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Afro-Brazilians and Yoruba families met and married. At home they speak Brazilian Portuguese and Yoruba, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Candomblé or Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 728 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Bahia Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

sulawesi.name: Bugis and Sulawesi peoples
sulawesi.strong: Makassar Commonwealth, Central Sulawesi, South Kalimantan
sulawesi.desc: In Celebes live the Bugis and Sulawesi peoples, a people of about 695 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Bugis, Makassarese, Toraja, and most are Sunni Muslim or Christian (Toraja). Their strongholds are Makassar Commonwealth, Central Sulawesi, South Kalimantan. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_bangkok.name: Khorat Bangkokians
f_bangkok.note: Thai and Lao families of the Khorat plateau after the Gulf rose
f_bangkok.desc: The people of Chao Phraya Commonwealth are the Khorat Bangkokians, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Thai and Lao families met and married. At home they speak Thai and Lao, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Theravada Buddhist by family, and many are secular. About 687 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Chao Phraya Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

garifuna.name: Garifuna and Miskito
garifuna.desc: The people of the Mosquito Coast are the Garifuna and Miskito, about 671 thousand strong in 2240. They were born where escaped Africans met the native peoples of the Caribbean coast. They speak Garifuna, Miskito, and most are Catholic or Dügü. Their strongholds are Olancho Canton. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

icelandic.name: Icelanders
icelandic.desc: The Icelanders are the people of Iceland, and in 2240 they number about 652 thousand. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. Their language is Icelandic. In faith most are Lutheran heritage or Ásatrú. They are strongest in Westfjords. The warming made their northern lands milder and busier than ever, and ice-free seas opened new ports.

f_turcogerman.name: Berlin Turco-Germans
f_turcogerman.faith: Protestant and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_turcogerman.desc: The Berlin Turco-Germans are a fusion people of 2240 from Brandenburg Commonwealth: German and Turkish Berliners, grown into one community. At home they speak German and Turkish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Protestant or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 640 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Brandenburg Commonwealth. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_istanbul_kurd.name: Anatolian Kurdo-Turks
f_istanbul_kurd.desc: In Ankara Capital Vilayet, Turks and Kurds families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Anatolian Kurdo-Turks. Their everyday speech mixes Turkish and Kurmanji. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 630 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Ankara Capital Vilayet. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

altai.name: Altaians
altai.desc: The Altaians are the people of the Altai mountains, and in 2240 they number about 624 thousand. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Their language is Altai. In faith most are Burkhanist or shamanist. They are strongest in Oirotia II, Oirotia, East Kazakhstan. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

minangkabau.name: Minangkabau
minangkabau.desc: The people of the West Sumatran highlands are the Minangkabau, about 615 thousand strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Minangkabau. In faith most are Sunni Muslim (matrilineal adat). Their strongholds are West Sumatra, South Sumatra. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

toubou.name: Toubou
toubou.strong: Murzuq Wilaya, Kufra Wilaya, Ajdabiya Wilaya
toubou.desc: The people of Tibesti are the Toubou, about 594 thousand strong in 2240. They are a Saharan people, heirs of the trans-desert caravan kingdoms around Lake Chad. They speak Tedaga, Dazaga, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Murzuq Wilaya, Kufra Wilaya, Ajdabiya Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_koryosaram.name: Koryo-Saram
f_koryosaram.faith: Secular and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_koryosaram.desc: The people of Almaty are the Koryo-Saram, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Koreans and Kazakhs families met and married. Their everyday speech mixes Korean and Kazakh. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 567 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Almaty. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

f_yekaterinburg.name: Ural Tatar-Bashkirs
f_yekaterinburg.desc: In Iset Commonwealth, Volga Tatars and Bashkirs families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Ural Tatar-Bashkirs. Their everyday speech mixes Tatar and Bashkir. In faith they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 543 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Iset Commonwealth, Arkaim-Tobol. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_peranakan.name: Straits Peranakans
f_peranakan.faith: Sunni Muslim and Secular families; many secular
f_peranakan.desc: The Straits Peranakans are a fusion people of 2240 from Johor: Malay and Han Singapore-Johor people, grown into one community. At home they speak Malay and Mandarin, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. They number about 541 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Johor. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

moors.name: Moors (Bidhan)
moors.strong: Oued Ed-Dahab Wilaya, Tiris Zemmour Wilaya, Tombouctou
moors.desc: The people of Mauritania are the Moors (Bidhan), about 528 thousand strong in 2240. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Hassaniya Arabic, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Oued Ed-Dahab Wilaya, Tiris Zemmour Wilaya, Tombouctou. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

temne_mende.name: Temne and Mende
temne_mende.desc: In Sierra Leone live the Temne and Mende, a people of about 510 thousand in 2240. They are an Atlantic people of West Africa, herders, farmers and traders of the savannah and the coast. Temne is their language, and most of them are Muslim or Christian. They are strongest in Northern. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

mari.name: Mari
mari.desc: In the Volga-Vyatka forests live the Mari, a people of about 508 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. They speak Mari, and most are Mari traditional faith or Orthodox. They are strongest in Kazan Commonwealth, Vyatka. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_lenatech.name: Lena Tech-Sakha
f_lenatech.note: Sakha and Korean river data-centre towns
f_lenatech.faith: Aar Aiyy (Sakha faith) and Secular families; many secular
f_lenatech.desc: In Olonkho, Sakha and Koreans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Lena Tech-Sakha. Their everyday speech mixes Sakha. In faith they are Aar Aiyy (Sakha faith) by family, and many are secular. About 494 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Olonkho. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

dogon.name: Dogon
dogon.desc: The people of Bandiagara are the Dogon, about 492 thousand strong in 2240. They are the Dogon of the Bandiagara cliffs, famous for their villages, masks and astronomy. Their language is Dogon. In faith most are Dogon faith or Muslim. They are strongest in Mopti. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

western_desert.name: Western Desert peoples
western_desert.desc: In Pitjantjatjara and Ngaanyatjarra lands live the Western Desert peoples, a people of about 490 thousand in 2240. They are part of the oldest continuous culture on Earth, more than fifty thousand years on the Australian continent. Their language is Pitjantjatjara. In faith most are Tjukurpa or Christian. Their strongholds are Auralia, Pilbara, Mparntwe Commonwealth. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

raramuri.name: Rarámuri and Wixárika
raramuri.desc: The people of Sierra Madre Occidental are the Rarámuri and Wixárika, about 486 thousand strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Rarámuri is their language, and most of them are Catholic with Native tradition. They are strongest in Chihuahua, Durango, Sonora. When the sea took Florida, the Gulf coast and lower Manhattan, millions of refugees moved inland, and the old heartland grew crowded, mixed and rich.

mennonite.name: Chaco Mennonites
mennonite.strong: Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Mato Grosso do Sul Captaincy
mennonite.desc: The Chaco Mennonites are the people of Central Chaco colonies, and in 2240 they number about 465 thousand. They descend from the Germanic-speaking peoples of northern Europe, whose languages and laws shaped much of the modern West. They speak Plautdietsch, and most are Mennonite. They are strongest in Presidente Hayes Captaincy, Mato Grosso do Sul Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

tiv.name: Tiv
tiv.desc: The Tiv are the people of the Benue valley, and in 2240 they number about 464 thousand. They belong to the Benue-Congo peoples of Nigeria's Middle Belt and Cross River, the cradle from which the Bantu once set out. They speak Tiv, and most are Christian. They are strongest in North. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_melbourne.name: Yarra Hellenic-Australians
f_melbourne.note: Anglo-Australian and Greek families of Melbourne
f_melbourne.language: Australian English and Greek (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_melbourne.faith: Secular and Greek Orthodox families; many secular
f_melbourne.desc: In Port Phillip, Anglo-Australians and Greeks families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Yarra Hellenic-Australians. At home they speak Australian English and Greek, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Greek Orthodox by family, and many are secular. About 457 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Port Phillip. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

estonian.name: Estonians
estonian.desc: The Estonians are the people of Estonia, and in 2240 they number about 456 thousand. Their Finnic tongue came west with Uralic-speaking hunters and farmers thousands of years ago and survived among the forests and lakes of the north. Estonian is their language, and most of them are Secular. They are strongest in Pirkanmaa. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

tuvan.name: Tuvans
tuvan.desc: In Tuva live the Tuvans, a people of about 448 thousand in 2240. Their Turkic forebears rode out of the steppes of Inner Asia over a thousand years ago and founded khanates and empires from China to the Danube. Tuvan is their language, and most of them are Tibetan Buddhist or shamanist. Their strongholds are Uriankhai, Khovd-Uvs Aimag. The warming of the twenty-second century turned their Siberian land from frontier into farmland and boom towns, and newcomers from Central Asia, China and Korea now live among them.

metis.name: Métis
metis.desc: In Prairie river valleys live the Métis, a people of about 440 thousand in 2240. They are a people of many origins, made by trade, plantations and migration. Their language is Michif. In faith most are Catholic. They are strongest in Assiniboia. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

munduruku.name: Munduruku and Tapajós peoples
munduruku.desc: The Munduruku and Tapajós peoples are the people of the Tapajós basin, and in 2240 they number about 432 thousand. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Munduruku is their language, and most of them are Traditional. Their strongholds are Para Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

ndebele.name: Ndebele
ndebele.desc: In Matabeleland live the Ndebele, a people of about 432 thousand in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Ndebele. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Matabeleland North. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

fijian.name: Fijians
fijian.desc: The people of Fiji are the Fijians, about 422 thousand strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Fijian is their language, and most of them are Methodist Christian. Their strongholds are Central-Northern. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

avar.name: Avars and Dagestani peoples
avar.desc: The Avars and Dagestani peoples are the people of Mountain Dagestan, and in 2240 they number about 404 thousand. They are an ancient mountain people of the Caucasus, whose many languages are found nowhere else on Earth. Their language is Avar and Dagestani languages. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Daghestan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

circassian.name: Circassians and Kabardians
circassian.desc: In Kuban, Kabardino-Balkaria live the Circassians and Kabardians, a people of about 395 thousand in 2240. They are an ancient mountain people of the Caucasus, whose many languages are found nowhere else on Earth. They speak Kabardian, Adyghe, and most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in Kuban Commonwealth. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

kalmyk.name: Kalmyks
kalmyk.desc: In the Caspian steppe live the Kalmyks, a people of about 393 thousand in 2240. Their ancestors once rode with the largest land empire in history, and the steppe still shapes their way of life. They speak Kalmyk, Russian, and most are Tibetan Buddhist. They are strongest in Tanais. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

nande.name: Nande and Kivu peoples
nande.desc: In North Kivu live the Nande and Kivu peoples, a people of about 376 thousand in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Kinande, Swahili, and most are Christian. They are strongest in North Kivu. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

basotho.name: Basotho
basotho.desc: The people of the Lesotho highlands are the Basotho, about 364 thousand strong in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Sesotho. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Free State. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

mordvin.name: Mordvins
mordvin.desc: The people of Moksha and Sura are the Mordvins, about 350 thousand strong in 2240. They belong to the Uralic peoples of the northern forests and tundra, among the oldest inhabitants of their lands. They speak Erzya, Moksha, and most are Orthodox Christian. They are strongest in Zhiguli-Simbirsk, Ukek-Burtasia. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

yanomami.name: Yanomami and Guiana Highland peoples
yanomami.strong: Amazonas Captaincy, Bolivar Department, Roraima Department
yanomami.desc: In the Guiana highlands live the Yanomami and Guiana Highland peoples, a people of about 328 thousand in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Yanomaman languages, and most are Shamanist. They are strongest in Amazonas Captaincy, Bolivar Department, Roraima Department. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

balinese.name: Balinese
balinese.desc: In Bali live the Balinese, a people of about 316 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Balinese, and most are Balinese Hindu. They are strongest in East Java. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_kamchatka.name: Kamchatka Pacific Mix
f_kamchatka.note: Russian and Japanese volcanic-coast fishers and geothermal crews
f_kamchatka.faith: Orthodox Christian and Shinto and Buddhist families; many secular
f_kamchatka.desc: The Kamchatka Pacific Mix are a fusion people of 2240 from Kamchadalia: Russian and Japanese volcanic-coast fishers and geothermal crews, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Russian and Japanese. In faith they are Orthodox Christian or Shinto or Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 312 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Kamchadalia, Olonkho II. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_uralokazakh.name: Uralo-Kazakhs
f_uralokazakh.note: Kazakh and Russian southern Urals steppe towns
f_uralokazakh.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_uralokazakh.desc: In Yaik, Kazakhs and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Uralo-Kazakhs. At home they speak Kazakh and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 308 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Yaik, Bashkiria, Aktobe. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

ewe.name: Ewe
ewe.desc: The people of Volta region are the Ewe, about 308 thousand strong in 2240. They are a Kwa people of the West African forest, heirs of kingdoms built on gold, kola and trade. Their language is Ewe. In faith most are Christian or Vodun. They are strongest in Northern-Brong-Ahafo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

chechen.name: Chechens and Ingush
chechen.desc: The Chechens and Ingush are the people of Chechnya, Ingushetia, and in 2240 they number about 303 thousand. They are an ancient mountain people of the Caucasus, whose many languages are found nowhere else on Earth. Chechen is their language, and most of them are Sufi Muslim. They are strongest in Daghestan. Their steppes and oases became corridors of trade and migration between a warming north and an overheated south.

tzotzil.name: Tzotzil and Tzeltal
tzotzil.desc: The people of the Chiapas highlands are the Tzotzil and Tzeltal, about 281 thousand strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Tzotzil is their language, and most of them are Catholic with Maya tradition. They are strongest in Chiapas. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_kuban.name: Kuban Cossack-Armenians
f_kuban.faith: Armenian Apostolic and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_kuban.desc: In Kuban Commonwealth, Armenians and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Kuban Cossack-Armenians. At home they speak Armenian and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Armenian Apostolic or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 276 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Kuban Commonwealth. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

indo_trini.name: Indo-Caribbeans
indo_trini.desc: The Indo-Caribbeans are the people of Trinidad, Guyana, and in 2240 they number about 268 thousand. Their language descends from the Sanskrit of ancient India, through the many tongues of the medieval kingdoms. They speak Trinidadian English, Bhojpuri heritage, and most are Hindu, Muslim or Christian. Their strongholds are Martinique-Guadeloupe. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

yucatec.name: Yucatec Maya
yucatec.desc: The Yucatec Maya are the people of Yucatán, and in 2240 they number about 218 thousand. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. Their language is Yucatec Maya. In faith most are Catholic or Maya tradition. Their strongholds are Chiapas. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_yukonkorean.name: Thaw-Belt Alaskans
f_yukonkorean.note: Alaskan and Korean farmers of the thawed interior
f_yukonkorean.language: American English and Korean (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_yukonkorean.faith: Christian and Secular families; many secular
f_yukonkorean.desc: In Alyeska Proper, Alaskans and Koreans families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Thaw-Belt Alaskans. Their everyday speech mixes American English and Korean. In faith they are Christian by family, and many are secular. About 217 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Alyeska Proper. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

maasai.name: Maasai
maasai.desc: The Maasai are the people of the Rift valley grasslands, and in 2240 they number about 182 thousand. They are a Nilotic people, cattle herders of the Nile and the Rift, tall, proud and stubborn about their land. Maa is their language, and most of them are Christian or Maasai tradition. They are strongest in Manyara-Singida. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_belem.name: Belém Delta Folk
f_belem.language: Brazilian Portuguese and Tupi-Guarani (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_belem.faith: Candomblé and Traditional families; many secular
f_belem.desc: The people of Para Captaincy are the Belém Delta Folk, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Afro-Brazilians and Amazonian peoples families met and married. At home they speak Brazilian Portuguese and Tupi-Guarani, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Candomblé or Traditional by family, and many are secular. They number about 173 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Para Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

ilocano.name: Ilocanos
ilocano.desc: The Ilocanos are the people of Northern Luzon, and in 2240 they number about 167 thousand. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Ilocano is their language, and most of them are Roman Catholic or Aglipayan. They are strongest in Luzonia. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_baikal.name: Baikal Buryat-Rus
f_baikal.faith: Tibetan Buddhist and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_baikal.desc: In Barguzin, Buryats and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Baikal Buryat-Rus. Their everyday speech mixes Buryat and Russian. In faith they are Tibetan Buddhist or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 164 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Barguzin. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

afar.name: Afar
afar.desc: In Danakil live the Afar, a people of about 163 thousand in 2240. They are a Cushitic people of the Horn of Africa, herders and traders on one of the oldest routes between Africa and Arabia. Their language is Afar. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Amhara, Somali. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

guyanese.name: Guyanese and Surinamese
guyanese.note: Guiana interior above the drowned coast
guyanese.strong: Roraima Department, Bolivar Department, Amapa Captaincy
guyanese.desc: The people of the Guiana interior above the drowned coast are the Guyanese and Surinamese, about 161 thousand strong in 2240. They are a people of many origins, made by trade, plantations and migration. Their language is Guyanese Creole. In faith most are Hindu, Christian or Muslim. They are strongest in Roraima Department, Bolivar Department, Amapa Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

f_tatarrus.name: Volga Tatar-Rus
f_tatarrus.note: Tatar and Russian Kazan river cities
f_tatarrus.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_tatarrus.desc: The people of Kazan Commonwealth are the Volga Tatar-Rus, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Volga Tatars and Russians families met and married. At home they speak Tatar and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 161 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Kazan Commonwealth. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

rakhine.name: Rakhine
rakhine.desc: The people of Arakan are the Rakhine, about 157 thousand strong in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. They speak Rakhine, and most are Theravada Buddhist. They are strongest in Sagaing. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

bemba.name: Bemba
bemba.desc: In Northern Zambia live the Bemba, a people of about 156 thousand in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Bemba. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Muchinga-Northern. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

wolof.name: Wolof and Senegambians
wolof.desc: The people of Senegal, Gambia are the Wolof and Senegambians, about 156 thousand strong in 2240. They are an Atlantic people of West Africa, herders, farmers and traders of the savannah and the coast. They speak Wolof, French, and most are Sufi Muslim. Their strongholds are Oued Ed-Dahab Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

yazidi.name: Yazidis
yazidi.desc: The Yazidis are the people of Sinjar and Shekhan, and in 2240 they number about 151 thousand. Their Iranian language links them to the old empires of Persia and to the horse peoples of the ancient steppe. They speak Kurmanji, and most are Yazidism. They are strongest in Al Anbar, Homs. Europe lost its low coasts and polders to the sea; the drowned lowlanders were resettled inland, and few regions are as unmixed as they were a century ago.

tlingit_yupik.name: Tlingit, Yup'ik and Alaska Natives
tlingit_yupik.desc: The people of Southeast and western Alaska are the Tlingit, Yup'ik and Alaska Natives, about 144 thousand strong in 2240. Their ancestors were in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived, and their nations survived conquest, disease and assimilation. They speak Tlingit, Yup'ik, English, and most are Christian or Native tradition. They are strongest in Alyeska Proper. The thaw opened the north of their land to farming, and new towns grew where there had been permafrost.

f_biocaboclo.name: Amazon Bio-Caboclos
f_biocaboclo.language: Tupi-Guarani and Brazilian Portuguese (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_biocaboclo.faith: Traditional and Catholic families; many secular
f_biocaboclo.desc: In Amazonas Captaincy, Amazonian peoples and Brazilians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Amazon Bio-Caboclos. At home they speak Tupi-Guarani and Brazilian Portuguese, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Traditional or Catholic by family, and many are secular. They number about 150 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Amazonas Captaincy. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

ndyuka.name: Maroons (Ndyuka and Saramaka)
ndyuka.desc: The Maroons (Ndyuka and Saramaka) are the people of the Suriname interior, and in 2240 they number about 132 thousand. They descend from Africans carried across the Atlantic in slavery, who made new peoples, faiths and music in the Americas. Their language is Ndyuka. In faith most are Winti or Christian. They are strongest in Amapa Captaincy, Sipaliwini Captaincy. The sea rose along their coasts and the cities climbed into the hills; the interior and its farms grew in importance.

greenlander.name: New Greenlanders
greenlander.note: Ice-free Greenland: Danish, Icelandic, Inuit and Canadian settlers
greenlander.desc: The New Greenlanders are the people of Nuuk Free Harbour, and in 2240 they number about 123 thousand. They speak Danish, Kalaallisut, English, and most are Lutheran heritage or secular. They are strongest in Nuuk Free Harbour, Tasiilaq, Ilulissat. The warming made their northern lands milder and busier than ever, and ice-free seas opened new ports.

chaga.name: Chaga and Pare
chaga.desc: In Kilimanjaro live the Chaga and Pare, a people of about 118 thousand in 2240. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. Their language is Chaga. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Coast, Manyara-Singida. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

kachin.name: Kachin
kachin.desc: In the Kachin hills live the Kachin, a people of about 116 thousand in 2240. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Jinghpaw. In faith most are Baptist and Catholic. Their strongholds are Kachin State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

samoan_tongan.name: Samoans and Tongans
samoan_tongan.desc: In Samoa, Tonga live the Samoans and Tongans, a people of about 112 thousand in 2240. Their ancestors were the Polynesian navigators who found every island of the Pacific with stars, swells and memory. Their language is Samoan. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Central-Northern. They live through the turbulent twenty-third century, a member people of the United Terran Commonwealth in the long Sol Conflict with Mars.

f_stpetersburg.name: Neva Highland Finno-Rus
f_stpetersburg.note: Russian and Finnic families moved up from the drowned Neva
f_stpetersburg.faith: Orthodox Christian and Lutheran heritage families; many secular
f_stpetersburg.desc: The Neva Highland Finno-Rus are a fusion people of 2240 from North Karelia: Russian and Finnic families moved up from the drowned Neva, grown into one community. At home they speak Russian and Finnish, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Orthodox Christian or Lutheran heritage by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in North Karelia. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_polykiwi.name: Polynesian Kiwis
f_polykiwi.note: Maori and Pacific Islander Auckland families
f_polykiwi.desc: The people of Te Whanganui Commonwealth are the Polynesian Kiwis, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Maori and Pacific Islanders families met and married. At home they speak Maori and Samoan, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Christian by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Te Whanganui Commonwealth, Northland. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

ganda.name: Baganda
ganda.desc: The Baganda are the people of Buganda, and in 2240 they number about 87 thousand. They are part of the great Bantu migration that carried farming and iron across central and southern Africa over three thousand years. They speak Luganda, and most are Christian. Their strongholds are Eastern Equatoria. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_bashkirspace.name: Ural Spacer Bashkirs
f_bashkirspace.faith: Sunni Muslim and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_bashkirspace.desc: The people of Bashkiria are the Ural Spacer Bashkirs, a new people of the twenty-third century, born where Bashkirs and Russians families met and married. At home they speak Bashkir and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Sunni Muslim or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Bashkiria. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

f_saltnomad.name: Qinghai Salt Nomads
f_saltnomad.faith: Tibetan Buddhist and Sunni Muslim families; many secular
f_saltnomad.desc: The Qinghai Salt Nomads are a fusion people of 2240 from Qinghai: Tibetan and Hui lithium-lake nomads, grown into one community. At home they speak Tibetan and Mandarin, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Tibetan Buddhist or Sunni Muslim by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Qinghai. They are the face of the new Earth: mixed, mobile, and loyal to their city before any old nation.

copt.name: Copts
copt.desc: The Copts are the people of Middle Egypt, and in 2240 they number about 66 thousand. Their Semitic language belongs to the family of Akkadian, Hebrew and Arabic, among the oldest written traditions in the world. They speak Egyptian Arabic, Coptic liturgy, and most are Coptic Orthodox. They are strongest in New Valley Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

nuba.name: Nuba
nuba.desc: The Nuba are the people of the Nuba mountains, and in 2240 they number about 60 thousand. They are the mountain peoples of Kordofan, more than a hundred communities on a few ranges of hills. Nuba languages is their language, and most of them are Muslim or Christian. Their strongholds are North Kordofan Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_tuvarus.name: Tuvan Steppe-Rus
f_tuvarus.faith: Tibetan Buddhist and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_tuvarus.desc: In Uriankhai, Tuvans and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Tuvan Steppe-Rus. Their everyday speech mixes Tuvan and Russian. In faith they are Tibetan Buddhist or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Uriankhai. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

f_hawaiipacific.name: Hawaiian Pacific Mix
f_hawaiipacific.faith: Christian and Shinto and Buddhist families; many secular
f_hawaiipacific.desc: The Hawaiian Pacific Mix are a fusion people of 2240 from Owhyhee Sector: Native Hawaiian and Japanese islanders, grown into one community. Their everyday speech mixes Hawaiian and Japanese. In faith they are Christian or Shinto or Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 150 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Owhyhee Sector. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

toraja.name: Toraja
toraja.desc: The Toraja are the people of the Sulawesi highlands, and in 2240 they number about 60 thousand. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Toraja is their language, and most of them are Protestant or Aluk To Dolo. They are strongest in Makassar Commonwealth. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_vladivostok.name: Golden Horn Sino-Rus
f_vladivostok.note: Han and Russian families of the Pacific port
f_vladivostok.faith: Secular and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_vladivostok.desc: The Golden Horn Sino-Rus are a fusion people of 2240 from Lukomorye: Han and Russian families of the Pacific port, grown into one community. At home they speak Mandarin and Russian, switching between the two in the same sentence; they are Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. They number about 150 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Lukomorye. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

acholi.name: Acholi and Lango
acholi.desc: The people of Northern Uganda are the Acholi and Lango, about 60 thousand strong in 2240. They are a Nilotic people, cattle herders of the Nile and the Rift, tall, proud and stubborn about their land. Their language is Acholi. In faith most are Christian. Their strongholds are Eastern Equatoria. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

f_karelian.name: Karelian Finno-Rus
f_karelian.faith: Lutheran heritage and Orthodox Christian families; many secular
f_karelian.desc: In Kalevala, Finns and Karelians and Russians families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Karelian Finno-Rus. Their everyday speech mixes Finnish and Russian. In faith they are Lutheran heritage or Orthodox Christian by family, and many are secular. About 150 thousand of them live in 2240, mostly in the big towns. You find them above all in Kalevala. Older relatives on both sides complain they have lost their roots; they answer that they grew new ones.

fur.name: Fur and Darfuri peoples
fur.strong: South Darfur Nome, North Darfur Nome
fur.desc: In Jebel Marra, Darfur live the Fur and Darfuri peoples, a people of about 60 thousand in 2240. They are a Nilo-Saharan people of the dry lands between the Nile and Lake Chad. Their language is Fur. In faith most are Sunni Muslim. They are strongest in South Darfur Nome, North Darfur Nome. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

serer.name: Serer
serer.desc: The people of Sine-Saloum are the Serer, about 60 thousand strong in 2240. They are an Atlantic people of West Africa, herders, farmers and traders of the savannah and the coast. Their language is Serer. In faith most are Muslim, Christian or Serer faith. They are strongest in Porto Novo. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

iban.name: Iban
iban.desc: In the Sarawak rivers live the Iban, a people of about 60 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Iban, and most are Christian or Iban tradition. Their strongholds are Sarawak River Commonwealth, Central Kalimantan. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

igorot.name: Igorot (Cordillerans)
igorot.desc: In Luzon Cordillera live the Igorot (Cordillerans), a people of about 60 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. They speak Ifugao, Kankanaey, Ibaloi, and most are Christian or ancestral. Their strongholds are Luzonia. The rising sea drowned the old coastal capitals, and their cities were rebuilt on the hills above the new shore.

f_lhasa.name: Lhasa Highland Synthesis
f_lhasa.note: Tibetan and Han plateau observatory towns
f_lhasa.language: Tibetan and Southwestern Mandarin (a bilingual 2240 creole)
f_lhasa.faith: Tibetan Buddhist and Secular families; many secular
f_lhasa.desc: In Lhasa Commonwealth, Tibetans and Southwestern Han families have lived side by side for so long that their grandchildren became a people of their own, the Lhasa Highland Synthesis. Their everyday speech mixes Tibetan and Southwestern Mandarin. In faith they are Tibetan Buddhist by family, and many are secular. They number about 150 thousand, almost all in cities. You find them above all in Lhasa Commonwealth. They are young, urban and ambitious, and the old communities they came from watch them with a mix of pride and suspicion.

soninke.name: Soninke
soninke.desc: The Soninke are the people of Upper Senegal, and in 2240 they number about 60 thousand. They descend from the Mande of the old Mali Empire, whose griots still keep its history in song. They speak Soninke, and most are Sunni Muslim. Their strongholds are Kayes, Hodh Ech Chargui Wilaya. The heat of the twenty-second century was hard on their land: many moved to the highlands, the coasts or abroad, and water became the measure of every town.

akha_lisu.name: Akha and Lisu
akha_lisu.desc: The Akha and Lisu are the people of the Golden Triangle hills, and in 2240 they number about 60 thousand. Their Tibeto-Burman language ties them to the peoples of the Himalaya and the high hills that run south into Burma. Their language is Akha. In faith most are Animist or Christian. They are strongest in Kachin State. The rising sea took the great river deltas, and millions of their people moved up into the hills, where they live crowded but alive.

yolngu.name: Yolngu
yolngu.desc: The Yolngu are the people of Arnhem Land, and in 2240 they number about 60 thousand. They are part of the oldest continuous culture on Earth, more than fifty thousand years on the Australian continent. They speak Yolŋu Matha, and most are Yolngu law or Christian. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

torres.name: Torres Strait Islanders
torres.desc: The people of Torres Strait, Cape York are the Torres Strait Islanders, about 60 thousand strong in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Torres Strait Creole. In faith most are Christian. The heat pushed their towns south and to the coasts, and the outback emptied further.

taiwanese_ind.name: Taiwanese Austronesians
taiwanese_ind.desc: In Central Mountain Range of Taiwan live the Taiwanese Austronesians, a people of about 60 thousand in 2240. They belong to the Austronesian seafarers who sailed out of Taiwan five thousand years ago and settled half the world's oceans. Their language is Amis. In faith most are Christian or ancestral.
